title: Iran's early attacks on Bahrain caught Navy families and sailors by surprise
summary: The scale and duration of Iran's response appeared to take the U.S. goverenment by surprise, three sources who were in Bahrain at the time told CBS News, in part because families hadn't yet been required to evacuate.
story: On the very first day of the war, Iran targeted the Navy's Middle East headquarters in Bahrain — before the U.S. government had evacuated all the military families based there. Some had to wait about a week or more to reach safety, according to multiple families who spoke to CBS News.
"You're definitely scared," one military spouse said. "As the week goes on, you wake up to ballistic missiles being fired. We went to sleep with the sound of ballistic missiles again."

Iranian missiles and drones targeted Bahrain consistently for several days after the war began, according to another spouse. The scale and duration of those attacks appeared to take the U.S. government by surprise, three sources who were in Bahrain at the time told CBS News, in part because families hadn't been required to evacuate until the war had already begun.

The military had anticipated some retaliation and had even evacuated the headquarters' buildings on the base, but "we weren't expecting that [scale]," one U.S. official said. And there were still several military families living off the base nearby.
One spouse said she could see the contrails of missiles and drones, and another heard explosions from attacks. CBS News granted anonymity to the spouses who feared retaliation for speaking.

No military personnel were killed in the attacks, but images that circulated on social media earlier this year — which sources say are authentic — show extensive damage to the base. One of the images shows an explosion during an attack on the first day of the war that targeted a key radar system.
Pentagon has not released a public estimated cost of damage

The U.S. military has not included the damage to bases in its cost estimates of the war so far because officials say they don't know what will be rebuilt, but acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao in a recent interview with The Epoch Times said Iran's retaliatory attacks "blew the hell out of Bahrain."

Since Naval Support Activity Bahrain officially became the headquarters for the Navy's Fifth Fleet in the '90s, it has served as a logistics hub for ships in the Middle East, including during the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan. According to the Navy's website, the facility serves approximately 8,300 military personnel, Defense Department civilian employees and their families.

The damage has impacted sailors at sea as well. Earlier this year, the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier faced food shortages as the Navy adjusted resupply routes away from Bahrain. The New York Times reported some supplies had to come through Diego Garcia, an island some 2,200 miles away in the Indian Ocean.

The extended route requires 14- to 18-day logistics cycles to deliver supplies to ships, according to a Pentagon Inspector General report. That's compared to 5 to 7 days from Bahrain, two former officials said. While there are other logistics hubs in the region, Bahrain was a key option before the war began.
Chief of Naval Operations Admiral Daryl Caudle, the Navy's top officer, at a town hall last month acknowledged the service has had to restructure how it supplies ships in the Middle East.
"There was some early learning there on getting the logistics process in place that I think now we have in a very good situation," Caudle said.

During the town hall, Caudle told a sailor who was evacuated from Bahrain that officials are working on retrieving belongings that were left behind because the Navy does not have imminent plans to return to the same level of footprint on the base.
"We're not getting back in there anytime soon, I just want to be completely honest with that," he said.

According to a Navy spokesperson, service members in Bahrain can ship their household goods and vehicles in person, and those outside Bahrain can designate a representative to act on their behalf, or coordinate travel back to Bahrain to move household goods and vehicles.
Some military families, service members and civilians in a bind

Since those opening days of the war, the Navy has helped evacuate about 1,450 service members and families from Bahrain. Many are now in a financial bind because they're paying for at least two households — one in Bahrain and another in the U.S.
"We have burned through our savings," one of the spouses told CBS News. "We have started having to take money out of our kids' college funds to pay down all the bills that we're incurring."
The Pentagon is providing benefits to reimburse housing costs in both places, but families told CBS News claims can take weeks to months to process.

In a statement, a Navy spokesperson said, "The Navy remains in close communication with all affected service members, affiliated civilians and families through command channels and continues to provide timely information, individual case management, and relocation support."

The spokesperson said families have until the end of November to transition from a safe haven to an established designated residence to continue receiving housing, relocation and separation entitlements.

Even if some families have not struggled financially through this process, all of them have been uprooted. Many were evacuated to Norfolk, Virginia, which is a Navy hub, or to Tampa, Florida, where U.S. Central Command's headquarters is located.
Blue Star Families, a non-profit that supports military families, provided supplies to evacuees in Tampa, according to Suzy Malloy, the executive director of the chapter in the Tampa Bay region.

"We gave these kids backpacks with school supplies," Malloy told CBS News. "We gave families brand new clothing, we gave them air fryers and crockpots so that they could cook in hotel rooms until they could adjust to something more permanent," like an Airbnb or temporary military housing.
Malloy said the evacuees are still in a bit of limbo but are starting to settle into Tampa.
"My opinion is [U.S. Central Command] and their family readiness program have done a remarkable job keeping the train on the tracks," Malloy said.
None of the families CBS News spoke to blamed the military for their challenges, but are frustrated with the overall situation — the evacuation and the uncertainty that has come after.
"Nobody expected this to go on so long," one of the spouses said.

title: Presley Gerber’s final hours at rehab in focus amid cause of death questions
summary: Presley Gerber's final hours draws questions. Police are investigating the 27-year-old model's death as a suspected overdose.
story: Presley Gerber, model and son of Cindy Crawford, has died at the age of 27. TMZ executive producer Michael Babcock discusses the investigation into Gerber's death and his past struggles with mental health and substance abuse.
Presley Gerber died Sunday, Sept. 20 – one day after entering the Resolutions Living rehabilitation facility in Santa Monica, Calif. He was 27.

Based off Wilshire Boulevard in an affluent Southern California community, the center is described as a co-ed home which "provides the structure" for residents on their journey to recovery from mental health, addiction, and co-occurring disorders through intensive outpatient programs of their choosing.

While it remained unclear why Cindy Crawford's son entered the center or what treatment he was receiving, wrongful death and personal injury attorney John J. Perlstein warned against jumping to conclusions of liability as the investigation continued into Gerber's death.
PRESLEY GERBER'S DEATH BEING INVESTIGATED AS 'A SUSPECTED OVERDOSE': POLICE
Presley Gerber died one day after entering a treatment facility in Los Angeles, Calif. (Getty Images)
"I just don't assume what the cause of death is or that the facility failed them or the family ... don't think the family wasn't doing everything they had to do," Perlstein told Fox News Digital.
"It seems like, you know, in these situations the families do so much for the sick person, the person who was addicted."
He added, "By all accounts, they were a very loving, good family, and it's just real sad circumstance. It certainly caught a lot of people's attention. I'll tell you that much."
Gerber, the only son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, died while staying at the rehabilitation facility, according to records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner.
KID ROCK CALLS PRESLEY GERBER’S DEATH A ‘TRAGEDY’ AS EX-GIRLFRIEND SAYS HE ‘DESERVED MORE TIME’

The treatment center's website says it draws "on our years of experience in addiction and mental health support," with "experienced staff has supported people with a wide variety of needs, from substance abuse and mental health, to trauma and eating disorders."
Cindy Crawford and husband Rande Gerber were seen at their late son Presley Gerber's home in Hollywood following his death at age 27. (RMBI/JOGA/JAPZ/Backgrid)
Gerber reportedly checked into the facility on Saturday night and died Sunday morning. Representatives for Resolutions Living did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Nicholas Kardaris, Ph.D., CEO and chief clinical officer of the New York Center for Living in Manhattan and a clinical professor at Stony Brook Medicine’s School of Social Welfare, cautioned against drawing conclusions from the fact that he died at a rehabilitation facility.
CINDY CRAWFORD’S SON PRESLEY GERBER SAID HE WAS ‘TERRIFIED’ IN RAW ADDICTION POST MONTHS BEFORE DEATH AT 27

As Gerber’s official cause of death has not yet been released, Kardaris — who has not treated Presley Gerber and is not connected to the case — noted that possible explanations could include an acute medical or cardiac event, an undiagnosed condition or a medication-related complication.
Presley Gerber was the only son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber. (Gilbert Flores/WWD via Getty Images)
Presley Gerber died Sunday of a suspected drug overdose, according to police. He was 27. (Paul Archuleta)
People in residential treatment facilities may have complex medical histories, and some conditions may not be immediately apparent when someone enters a program.
"Younger people can sometimes die suddenly, and we don’t know whether they had an underlying medical issue," Kardaris said.
"It’s not impossible to have a medication-related event, particularly if someone has an underlying heart disorder," he continued. "Certain medications can trigger a cardiac episode."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
He added, "People are in rehab because they’re struggling with addiction. It doesn’t mean they’re cured of their addiction."

Another potential risk during rehab is withdrawal itself, which can range from uncomfortable to life-threatening depending on the substance involved and the person’s level of physical dependence, according to Kardaris.
Presley Gerber's death investigation is ongoing with limited information available, according to the medical examiner. (Jeff Spicer/Getty Images for Tommy Hilfiger)
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
"People can die from withdrawal, but the substances that are most dangerous to withdraw [from] without proper medical supervision are benzodiazepines, such as Valium or Xanax, and alcohol," he said.
The deputy medical examiner (DME) told Fox News Digital that "the investigation is still ongoing and there is limited information available," and his cause of death has not yet been released.
The DME is in "the early stages of investigating the death of 27-year-old model Presley Gerber and limited information is currently available," according to a statement from the department.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"A deputy medical examiner performed an examination today and the cause and manner of death have been deferred, which means additional testing and/or studies were requested in order to make a determination."
Presley Gerber had been candid about past addiction issues. (Victor Boyko/Getty Images for Balmain)
They added, "Due to the ongoing death investigation, the DME cannot disclose what testing and/or studies were requested. Deferred cases can take a few months before a cause of death is determined."
Santa Monica Police Department officials are investigating the death as "a suspected overdose," according to a release from the department.
Officers responded to a report of a possible overdose at approximately 9:35 a.m., Sunday, Sept. 20. Upon arrival, officers located an adult male who was deceased.
At this time, there is no indication of foul play, and Gerber's case remains open. The facility has not been accused of wrongdoing.

A representative for the family told Fox News Digital, "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time."

title: Ella Langley says 'Choosin' Texas' success is 'changing my life' after her song breaks Mariah Carey's record
summary: Ella Langley celebrated a career-defining milestone after “Choosin’ Texas" spent its 23rd week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.
story: Ella Langley speaks about her deep appreciation for supporters and how their connection transformed her path, while attending the 2026 iHeartRadio Music Awards.
Ella Langley knew "Choosin' Texas" was special. Even she couldn't have predicted just how far it would go.

On Tuesday night, Langley took to Instagram to celebrate making Billboard Hot 100 history this week when "Choosin' Texas" logged its 23rd week at No. 1, surpassing Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You" for the longest reign at the top of the chart.

"I'm genuinely trying to find the words to explain what's going on in my brain today," Langley began her video. "What? I don't know. Thank you so much. Thank you for loving this song, for listening to it. I feel like… I just don't even know what to say at this point. I'm running out of hyperboles to describe how I feel, so I will just let my dog in the background show you his excitement," she continued as her dog barked.
Ella Langley topped the Billboard Hot 100 charts for the 14th week in a row with her "Choosin' Texas" anthem. (John Schearer)

"Just thank you. Thank you so much. It's changing my life. It's changing the lives of the writers of this song. It's changing the lives of my family, and it is truly growing an atmosphere for something I'm gonna be able to do the rest of my life and I just… today doesn't feel like a real thing," Langley said. "It feels fake and somebody's going to come in and be like 'haha we're kidding the whole time just kidding.'"
ELLA LANGLEY SEEMINGLY FIRES BACK AFTER DOJA CAT'S BRUTAL TAKE ON HER CHART-TOPPING HIT
"I'm really excited to just experience a moment like this in my life," she said.
The country music star told her fans that she was going to celebrate tonight before ending with, "Choosin' T… that's the one huh?"
In a resurfaced interview with Billboard from March, when the song was still climbing, Langley admitted its success had already surpassed anything she imagined when she wrote it.
"When we wrote it, I knew it was going on the record. I honestly knew it was going to be the lead single," Langley told Billboard.

"And we love that song, but I don't think I could have ever imagined what's happening with it right now," she continued. "Like I said, every day I wake up, and it's doing something that I didn't even know was a goal that I could have had."
"It's just nuts," Langley added. "It's crazy to see the ownership that the fans have taken over it. And the different demographics of people listening to the song is so cool."
What seemed unimaginable to Langley in March has since become historic.
ELLA LANGLEY'S 'CHOOSIN' TEXAS' SPENDS 15 WEEKS AT NUMBER ONE ON THE BILLBOARD HOT 100
"Choosin' Texas" first entered the Hot 100 in November 2025, became Langley's first top 10 in January and reached No. 1 for the first time in February.
The song has also spent 41 weeks at No. 1 on Billboard's Hot Country Songs chart.
Long before it became a record breaker, however, "Choosin' Texas" began with a story about a kangaroo.
Langley recalled writing the song during her first songwriting retreat with country superstar Miranda Lambert and two other writers.

"So, I was on a writer's retreat with Miranda," Langley explained in the resurfaced Billboard interview. "This is our first time that we had written together, and obviously we were there with two others."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Ella Langley performs onstage during the 59th Annual Country Music Association Awards at Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tenn., on Nov. 19, 2025. (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images)
Billboard credits Langley, Lambert, Luke Dick and Joybeth Taylor as the four co-writers of "Choosin' Texas."
Langley said Lambert began telling her a story about a pet kangaroo.
"I learned at a young age she had a pet kangaroo and I wanted to ask her about it," Langley recalled. "So, I was like, 'Tell me about this kangaroo that you had. I need to know.'"
ELLA LANGLEY'S TEXAS PHOTO DUMP SENDS COUNTRY MUSIC FANS INTO A FRENZY ONLINE ON INSTAGRAM
Lambert told the group about once being pulled over with the kangaroo riding in the passenger seat and a dog in the back.
Advertisement
"She said she got pulled over and the kangaroo ended up getting her out of a ticket, but she's like, 'Of course, I had Texas plates on, too,'" Langley recalled.
ELLA LANGLEY JOINS MUSIC ROYALTY WITH 'INSANE' MILESTONE FOR 'CHOOSIN' TEXAS'
Ella Langley performs onstage at the Billboard Women in Music 2026 held at the Hollywood Palladium on April 29, 2026, in Los Angeles, Calif. (Rich Polk/Billboard via Getty Images)
That was enough to spark the song.
"And I went, 'Well, she's from Texas, I can tell,'" Langley said. "And just from that phrase, it kind of all hit us."
According to Langley, the melody came almost immediately, with Lambert helping develop the story behind it.
"And 45 minutes later, we had that song written," Langley said. "And it was just, it was such a cool experience."
Lambert's involvement didn't end in the writing room.
Langley told Billboard that the country superstar was executive producing her next record and had become someone she could turn to for advice.

"There's not a rulebook to this job," Langley said. "So to be able to have someone like her to ask questions and think, you know, is it, should I be doing this? She's like, 'Hell yeah, you should be doing this.'"
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Miranda Lambert and Ella Langley pose in the winner's walk during the 61st Academy of Country Music Awards. (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for ACM)
Even Lambert was surprised by what was happening with "Choosin' Texas."
"My team's calling me every day freaking out about this song," Langley recalled Lambert telling her.
At the time of the March interview, the song had reached No. 5 on the Hot 100.
"How crazy is that?" Langley said.
"And for me, like, what, me? You mean me?"
Six months later, "Choosin' Texas" stands alone as the longest-running No. 1 song in Hot 100 history.
Langley's historic week comes as she continues performing across the country.

"Oxford, Athens & Jacksonville ❤️," she captioned the Instagram post.

The images showed Langley performing with her guitar, posing near an Ole Miss sign in a dress and red boots, holding a snake and preparing backstage in front of a lighted mirror. Another captured an older couple dancing during her show.

title: Javier Bardem slammed for targeting Pink over Macklemore comments: 'The left is eating itself'
summary: Actor Javier Bardem promoted a petition to remove Pink as a UNICEF ambassador, drawing fierce pushback from Michael Rapaport and Selma Blair.
story: Fox News correspondent CB Cotton reports on singer Pink criticizing rapper Macklemore over his pro-Palestinian remarks at a concert on ‘Fox Report.’
Actor Javier Bardem has stepped into the middle of the controversy surrounding Pink, Macklemore and the Israel-Gaza conflict — and is now taking heat for it.

The "No Country for Old Men" star shared multiple posts to his Instagram Stories Monday urging followers to sign a Change.org petition demanding that Pink be removed as a UNICEF ambassador, according to Reuters.
The petition Bardem promoted, titled "Remove Pink as a UNICEF Ambassador," calls on the organization to remove the singer from her position.
ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO ‘BUILD A BRIDGE’ OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO
Javier Bardem promoted a petition calling for Pink to be removed from her UNICEF ambassador role following controversy involving Macklemore's pro-Palestinian performance. (Getty Images)
Supporters argue that Pink’s comments are "incompatible with the role of a UNICEF Ambassador" and say ambassadors should promote "peace, understanding, and humanitarian values above personal biases."
The petition urges UNICEF to "take decisive action and remove Pink as an ambassador," arguing that the organization must remain committed to all children regardless of "nationality or heritage."

Bardem’s move drew pushback from fans and fellow celebrities who questioned why the actor was backing an effort to strip Pink of her UNICEF title over comments she made after Macklemore’s pro-Palestinian concert appearance.
Michael Rapaport delivered one of the most blistering responses, mocking Bardem as a "tattletale" and accusing the actor of going after Pink through a petition rather than confronting her directly.
He wrote in an Instagram caption: "Javier Bar-Dumb Dumb initiated,signed & is promoting a petition to have singer PINK removed as a UNICEF Ambassador. He’s is Bullying a Proud Jewish Woman."

Rapaport continued in his video: "Javier Bar-Dumb Dumb. Javier Bardem, what the f--- are you doing, you little tattle-tale? Hall monitor … you are a grown man, a grown f---ing man. Pink is a grown woman. You're both world-famous. If you have a problem with what she said, call her. Sit her down, have a coffee, look her dead in the face and express all and any frustrations and questions you have … instead you sign a petition, like a little b---- to have her removed as a UNICEF ambassador. What the f--- is wrong with you?"
PINK HITS BACK AMID BACKLASH FOR CRITICIZING MACKLEMORE'S PRO-PALESTINIAN CONCERT REMARKS
Michael Rapaport criticized Javier Bardem after the actor promoted a petition targeting Pink over her response to the controversy surrounding Macklemore. (Noam Galai/Getty Images)

Selma Blair also weighed in in the comment section, writing: "Why would anyone want this great removed from unicef for human , humble and loving words? This makes no sense. I would think the terrifically talented actor man would worry about his own incredible life more. And allow love to flow. And listen to everybody. Not just his echo chamber. But alas."
Bardem's decision to promote the petition also drew criticism from social media users, with commenters questioning why the actor was pushing for Pink's removal over her comments.

One commenter wrote: "I'm not a big Pink fan...I like her music okay, but she was one of the many performers who actually did ads for Big Pharma pushing the vax during covid. That said, who the hell is Bardem to cancel her? The left is eating itself."
Meanwhile, supporters of Bardem's position also commented on the petition.

"Pink chose her and her rich friends' discomfort was more important than people's lives," one commenter wrote, adding that if UNICEF does not "stand with Gaza now and remove Pink," then "the world is a much darker place."

Another argued, "No ambassador can call attention to important issues while actively ignoring and deliberately misunderstanding and misrepresenting the conditions in Palestine. Pink has shown herself incapable of even acknowledging what is clear to the world, and is not fit to serve UNICEF."

A third commenter questioned how Pink could remain a UNICEF advocate while, in their view, failing to support "basic human rights and free speech for all people, especially those in Gaza, the Sudan and the Congo."
Fox News Digital reached out to Bardem, UNICEF and Pink for comment.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Ed Sheeran and Macklemore attend the 2013 MTV Video Music Awards at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York City. (Kevin Mazur/WireImage)
MACKLEMORE DONATES $1M TO PALESTINIAN AID ORGANIZATIONS AFTER ED SHEERAN TOUR FALLOUT
The petition Bardem promoted centers on Pink’s response to Macklemore’s appearance with Ed Sheeran at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sept. 4.
Macklemore performed "Hind's Hall," his song supporting Palestinians, while repeatedly chanting "Free Palestine" as images related to Gaza appeared on a screen behind him.
The performance sparked criticism from the @Stop_Antisemitism Instagram account, which accused Macklemore of using the concert to push "anti-Israel propaganda."
Pink faced backlash after reposting the criticism and subsequently issued her own lengthy explanation.
Pink faced backlash after reposting criticism of Macklemore's performance of "Hind's Hall" at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Christopher Polk/NBC/NBCU Photo Bank)
"I’ve been quiet in my own words for a week, which you know isn’t like me. So here they are," she wrote on social media.
"I was born a Jew," Pink continued. "I didn’t pick it, and I’ve never hidden it."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
She also addressed her position on the conflict.

"Of course I don’t speak for Israel, or for any government. I never have," Pink wrote. "What I said in October 2023 is still exactly what I believe: Hamas is a terrorist organization. Palestinians deserve a future that honors their humanity and their aspirations. Protecting innocent life comes first, everywhere, and nobody should ever celebrate the death of a child. Anybody’s child."
Pink also cited her years of work with UNICEF, saying she had spent time with children "on both sides of that fence."
"I’m not going to litigate a complex war in an Instagram caption, and I’m not going to recite anybody’s slogan to earn back a follower," she wrote.

Pink went on to explain that what she was "reacting to" was Macklemore himself. She recalled him performing his song "Same Love" at the Grammys in 2014, and how she cheered on the message, but "Four months later Macklemore put on a hooked nose, a black beard and a bowl cut, performed in it, and called it a 'random costume.'"
Pink wrote in her statement about Macklemore that she'd been working with UNICEF for years. (Lorne Thomson/Redferns)

"Every Jew I know knew exactly what it was. The same love, it turned out, had a guest list, and we weren’t on it. But he apologized, and I let it go, because that’s what we do. We let it go. Then last weekend he stood in front of a stadium full of music-loving families, with violent images from a war on the screens, dedicated a song to the movement of his choice, and then took the mic to tell all of the Jews in the stadium that it wasn’t about them."
She added, "You don’t get to decide that for us."

"That’s what prompted my repost," she wrote. "Not 'Free Palestine,' and not anyone’s right to say it. I have never asked for another artist to be silenced and I’m not asking now. I don’t need anyone fired, and I don’t need a refund. What I need is to be able to say, as a Jewish mom, 'that scared me, and it scared people I love,' without being told our fear is just propaganda, and without being told I’m somehow cool with genocide because I noticed?"
Macklemore performed "Hind's Hall" during Ed Sheeran's concert at MetLife Stadium on Sept. 4, where the rapper repeatedly chanted "Free Palestine." (Kieran Frost/Redferns)

The controversy surrounding Macklemore's stage appearance continued after the MetLife Stadium performance. Macklemore later posted a video on Instagram addressing the crowd and said performing on Sheeran's tour gave him the opportunity to deliver his "Free Palestine" message to a massive audience.
Macklemore doubled down in the caption and wrote, "Wanting all humans to be treated equal should never be controversial."
He was later dropped from the tour altogether after venues told the tour's promoters that they would "not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup."

title: Taylor Swift has fans spiraling over cryptic countdown and ‘hidden in plain sight’ clues

title: Presley Gerber dead at 27: What to know about Cindy Crawford, Rande Gerber's family
summary: Presley Gerber died at age 27 while staying at a rehabilitation facility, putting a renewed spotlight on Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber's family.
story: Presley Gerber, model and son of Cindy Crawford, has died at the age of 27. TMZ executive producer Michael Babcock discusses the investigation into Gerber's death and his past struggles with mental health and substance abuse.
Presley Gerber’s death has put renewed focus on one of the entertainment industry’s most famous families.

Gerber, the only son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, died Sept. 20 at age 27 while staying at a rehabilitation facility, according to records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. His cause of death has not been released.

"The family is in total shock right now. They are saddened beyond words," a source told People magazine. "Kaia [Gerber] loved that Presley was so open about his struggles; his family was so proud that he was finding strength in helping others."
PRESLEY GERBER, SON OF CINDY CRAWFORD AND RANDE GERBER, DEAD AT 27
A representative for the family told Fox News Digital, "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time."
Presley Gerber, pictured with Kaia Gerber, Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber in May, died on Sunday. He was 27.  (Gilbert Flores/WWD via Getty Images)

The Gerber-Crawford family has long attracted attention because of its connections to fashion, Hollywood, business and celebrity culture. At the center of the family are Cindy and Rande, who raised Presley and their daughter, model and actress Kaia Gerber.
Cindy Crawford is one of the most recognizable faces in the modeling industry.  (Olivia Wong/FilmMagic)
Cindy rose to fame in the 1980s and became one of the most recognizable faces in fashion.

She appeared on hundreds of magazine covers and worked with designers and brands around the world. Crawford was also part of the "Big Five" supermodels, a group that included Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, Christy Turlington and Tatjana Patitz.

Actress and model Cindy Crawford sits on a Harley-Davidson motorcycle on the set of a Pepsi commercial wearing a black leather jacket surrounded by actors dressed as policemen in 1992 in Los Angeles, California.  (Roxanne McCann)

Her work reached beyond the runway, with appearances in advertising campaigns, music videos, television programs and movies. Cindy later expanded her career into business, launching beauty, skin care and wellness ventures while continuing to work as a model and brand ambassador.

(L-R) Kaia Gerber, Rande Gerber, model Cindy Crawford and Presley Gerber attend Rock4EB! 2015 with Ed Sheeran and David Spade on Nov. 15, 2015, in Malibu, California. (Todd Williamson/Getty Images for EB Kids)
While Cindy was becoming a fashion icon, Rande established his own career in hospitality and nightlife.

He founded the Gerber Group, which operated bars, lounges and restaurants in hotels and entertainment venues around the world. His businesses helped make him a prominent figure in the hospitality industry.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Rande later joined forces with actor George Clooney and real estate developer Mike Meldman to create Casamigos tequila. The brand began as a private venture among friends before becoming a major spirits company.

George Clooney, Amal Clooney, Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber attend the Clooney Foundation for Justice Inaugural Albie Awards at New York Public Library on Sept. 29, 2022. (Getty Images for Albie Awards)

Rande’s friendship and business partnership with Clooney also connected the two families. Cindy and Rande built a home next door to Clooney’s property in Los Cabos, Mexico, with the two residences designed as neighboring villas.

The families remained close in their business and social circles. Rande and Cindy later purchased an apartment in the same New York City building as George and Amal Clooney, according to the New York Post.
KAIA GERBER OWNS 'NEPO BABY' STATUS WHILE QUESTIONING OTHER CELEBRITY KIDS: 'SHOW ME WHY YOU DESERVE THIS JOB'
Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber welcomed Presley in 1999 and Kaia in 2001. (Bruce Glikas/FilmMagic)
Cindy and Rande married in 1998 and welcomed Presley in 1999. Their daughter, Kaia, was born in 2001.

The couple has largely kept their family life private, choosing to raise their children away from the constant spotlight surrounding their careers. However, both Presley and Kaia eventually followed their mother into the fashion industry.
In a recent interview with Porter magazine, Cindy discussed the challenges of becoming an empty nester as both of her children established homes and careers of their own.
"When they become adults, all of a sudden you’re like, okay, I’ve got to back off here. It might not be the way I would do it, but you know," she said.
Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber married in 1998. (Getty Images)
She described the transition as an opportunity to reconnect with Rande after nearly three decades of marriage.

"When you get married, you talk about what kind of family you want or where we’re going to live. But no one ever talks about what this phase looks like, empty nesting, because it’s so far away you can’t even imagine it," she said. "But it’s an opportunity for us to redefine our relationship."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Presley Gerber was the only son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber. (Alberto Rodriguez/Variety via Getty Images)

"What do we want to do? Do we want to travel, do we not want to travel?" she continued. "We haven’t answered those questions yet, but we’re asking the questions, and it’s fun trying to figure that out together."
Cindy also expressed hope that she would one day become a grandmother.

"One thing I’m really looking forward to is being a grandmother," she said. "I’m at the age where a lot of my friends are starting to have grandkids, and even though I don’t think either one of my kids is close, I do hope I get to experience that, because it looks really fun."
Presley signed with a modeling agency at 15 years old.  (Victor Boyko/Getty Images for Balmain)
Presley was born in Beverly Hills, California, in 1999. He signed with IMG Models at age 15 and began building a career in fashion.
He walked in runway shows for designers including Moschino and Dolce & Gabbana and appeared in campaigns for brands including Calvin Klein.

Presley also worked alongside Kaia, who was establishing her own career in the fashion industry. In 2018, he told People magazine that having his sister in the business made modeling "a lot less lonely."
Kaia Gerber also began modeling as a young girl.  (FilmMagic)
Kaia began modeling as a child and later signed with IMG Models, the same agency that represented her brother and mother.
She quickly became one of the most recognizable young faces in fashion, walking in runway shows and appearing in campaigns for major designers and brands.
Kaia has also pursued acting. Her credits include appearances in "American Horror Story," "Bottoms," and "The Shards."
Although she has often been compared to her mom, Kaia has spoken about developing her own identity and career outside of her mother’s legacy.
Cindy has said she was proud of the relationship between her two children.
The mother-daughter duo share a similar resemblance.  (Cindy Ord/Getty Images)
"Nothing makes, I think, a parent prouder than when your kids like each other and love each other," she said during a People magazine interview.

Presley was known to speak publicly about his mental-health and addiction struggles. Although Cindy and Rande generally kept those issues private, they publicly supported him when he chose to discuss his experiences.
In March, Presley shared a post about undergoing an "ibogaine flood dose" at a wellness clinic in Cancún, Mexico.
Cindy commented on the post, writing, "You are a warrior! Walked thru the fire to find yourself! So proud!"
The family often publicly supported one another.  (Getty Images)
Rande also shared a message of support.
"I’m so proud of you and your courage," he wrote. "Facing what’s hard takes real strength, and watching you find your way back to yourself is everything. I love you so much."
A source told Page Six that what was seen online wasn't just an act.

"They were so close," a source told the outlet. "What you saw online and in the press wasn’t just for that purpose. They were a tight-knit family and Kaia and Presley were more than just siblings. Cindy has to be beyond gutted."

(L-R) Rande Gerber, Cindy Crawford and Presley Walker Gerber attend Chanel Dinner Celebrating our Majestic Oceans, A Benefit for NRDC at Private Residence on June 2, 2018, in Malibu, California. A source told People magazine, "The family is in total shock right now. They are saddened beyond words." (Stefanie Keenan/WireImage)
Kaia praised her brother’s willingness to be honest about his struggles in a Vogue cover story published in August, about a month before his death.

"My parents for most of our lives were very, very private and didn’t share anything — and now we have this absolute teacher, my brother, who says, ‘I’m gonna be very human for everyone,’" Kaia said. "There’s only so much you can hide from the world."
She also described the impact of his addiction on the entire family.

"When something like that happens in a family, it kind of levels everyone," Kaia said.
A source told People magazine that Cindy and Rande were never "two absent Hollywood parents."

"Cindy and Rande could not have been more supportive of Presley," the source said. "They were always there for him and did everything they could to help him. The family has always been incredibly close, and Presley was deeply loved."

title: Hayden Panettiere cause of death revealed

Hayden Panettiere died from the toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol and quetiapine, according to the Greenville County Coroner's Office. The manner of death was ruled an accident.

"The Greenville County Coroner’s Office responded to the scene and initiated a parallel investigation with the Greenville City Police Department. The decedent has been identified as Hayden Leslie Panettiere, 36, of California. Panettiere was found unresponsive inside the residence, where she had been temporarily staying.
"An autopsy was completed by a Board Certified Forensic Pathologist. At autopsy no signs of trauma were discovered that would have contributed to the death."
"The cause of death has been ruled as toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol, and Quetiapine. The manner of death has been ruled accident."

title: ‘Charlie’s Angels’ star Jaclyn Smith lived apart from her husband for 17 years during their 35-year love story
summary: Jaclyn Smith's memoir details her four marriages, a chance encounter with Warren Beatty, and the long-distance love that lasted 35 years.
story: Jaclyn Smith tells Fox News Digital the one powerful force behind her ageless appearance at the Paley Honors Spring Gala in New York.
For Jaclyn Smith, love wasn't waiting in Hollywood — it walked into her father's hospital room.

The actress, who starred as Kelly Garrett on the TV series "Charlie's Angels" from 1976 to 1981, recently penned a memoir, "I Once Knew a Guy Named Charlie." In it, the 80-year-old revealed that she and her fourth husband, Dr. Brad Allen, lived apart for 17 of their 35 years together.

Smith first met Allen, 72, when he helped perform her father's heart surgery in 1991. About two years later, Allen took a job at the University of Illinois in Chicago. He spent the next 17 years there while Smith continued living in Los Angeles.
‘CHARLIE’S ANGELS’ STAR JACLYN SMITH SAYS BEAUTY SECRET ISN’T MAKEUP OR DIET AFTER FANS PRAISE YOUTHFUL GLOW
Dr. Brad Allen and Jaclyn Smith attend the Farrah Fawcett Foundation Tex-Mex Fiesta Benefit on Oct. 20, 2022, in Dallas, Texas. (Getty Images for Farrah Fawcett Foundation)

"It's true, the greatest love comes when you're least looking for it," Smith told Fox News Digital. "He operated on my dad. I remember he walked into the room, and he looked like the guys I grew up with, clean cut and just collegiate. He looked like just the guy down the street. And he was so good to my parents."
After three divorces, Smith said motherhood changed everything. While a romance quickly blossomed, she wasn't willing to gamble on love again. This time, she wouldn't rush walking down the aisle.
"Brad and I finally said 'I do!' in Los Angeles on Oct. 11, 1997," Jaclyn Smith wrote in her memoir. (Courtesy of Jaclyn Smith)

"You see, when I met Brad, I had two children," she explained. "It was no longer me going, 'OK, my heart's beating out of my chest, and I'm going to get married right away.' It had to be a three-way decision."
WATCH: CHARLIES ANGELS STAR JACLYN SMITH, 80, REVEALS SECRET TO HER AGELESS LOOK

"Ultimately, we commuted for 17 years," she continued. "We married after seven years. And when we got married, we really knew one another. We knew each other's families. We knew our priorities. We knew what we expected in life. And that is important in any relationship."
Jaclyn Smith is seen here with her family today. (Courtesy of Jaclyn Smith)

Smith and Allen married in 1997. Smith's daughter, then 11 years old, was the maid of honor, People magazine reported. According to the outlet, her son, then 15, gave her away. The outlet reported that Allen closed the distance for good in 2009.
For Smith, the true test of marriage isn't only falling in love — it's building a life together.

Jaclyn Smith says love and family are behind her youthful glow at 80, as she reunited with Kate Jackson for the 50th anniversary of "Charlie's Angels" earlier this year. (Tina Thorpe / Disney; Harry Langdon / Getty Images)

"We see life the same rather than your heart just beating out," she said. "Yes, it beats out of your chest at first, but then you have to get down to the nitty-gritty of what makes the world go round, that day-to-day living."
Allen supported Smith through her 2002 breast cancer diagnosis. The star is now cancer-free after undergoing a lumpectomy and radiation.
Jaclyn Smith attends the Farrah Fawcett Foundation 2025 Tex-Mex Fiesta at The Rustic on Oct. 30, 2025 in Dallas, Texas. (Omar Vega/Getty Images for Farrah Fawcett Foundation)
Smith first married Roger Davis, then a star of "Dark Shadows," in 1968. He proposed to Smith after two dates.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Jaclyn Smith attends "Jaclyn Smith in Conversation: Beyond Charlie's Angels" at 92NY in New York City on Sept. 9, 2026. (Getty Images)

Two years into their relationship, Smith wrote that she was walking with a friend in New York City to look at an apartment she and Davis were considering renting when she ran into Warren Beatty. The actor asked her to interview for a role in a film he was working on. But moments later, Davis appeared and told Beatty that Smith only did commercials.

Smith wrote she later learned that while she was talking to Beatty, Davis was upstairs having sex with their real estate agent in the apartment. Smith split from Davis after finding him with another woman on their fourth wedding anniversary.
"I Once Knew a Guy Named Charlie: A Memoir" by Jaclyn Smith is available now. (Gallery Books)

"I knew my marriage wasn't everything I dreamed," Smith said. "I knew there were problems from day one. I think I have a line in the book about love masquerading as foundation, attraction as permanence. And I came from a background of you didn't live with people. It was the '50s. I didn't want to disappoint my parents. And I really believed in that picket fence. Why wouldn't this be great?"
Jaclyn Smith was a successful model before "Charlie's Angels" came calling. (2008 American Broadcasting Companies, Inc.)

"To fall in love, get married and go the distance — I think that's a wonderful thing," she continued. "There is a bond when that truly happens. I've seen my brother, who fell in love at age 19 or 20, get married. They went on to have three children and were together until my brother passed away. So I do think that's pretty wonderful when that happens. It just didn't for me. And a lot of it was my innocence. I was a romantic. I didn't look beneath the paper. It just looked good on paper. It looked perfect."
Smith said that while they were both actors, her values and Davis' values were vastly different.
Jaclyn Smith is seen here with her two children, circa 1988. (Courtesy of Jaclyn Smith)

"You tend to overlook that big statement, 'love is blind,'" Smith said. "But attraction is blind. Love comes from all your lessons. And listen, today is different. Nothing is left to the imagination on these dating sites. I'm glad I didn't start out at that point. I think values are so important, to share the same values. People tend to overlook that initially and think it's a sure shot."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Jaclyn Smith attends the 2026 Paley Honors Spring Gala at The Plaza Hotel in New York City on May 14, 2026. (Theo Wargo/Getty Images)
When asked if she regretted not taking a chance to work with Beatty, Smith replied, "Things happen for a reason."

"I never had a definite plan for my career," she explained. "I was never overly driving or ambitious. I just wanted to take what came my way at the time. That was shocking to me when Warren Beatty remembered my name and I didn't know too much about Warren Beatty except I loved his movie 'Bonnie and Clyde.'"
Faye Dunaway and Warren Beatty are seen here as Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow in the 1967 film "Bonnie and Clyde," directed by Arthur Penn. (Getty Images)

"I think whether I did the James Bond movie or the Warren Beatty movie, I think what happened in my life. Everything's unpredictable," Smith said. "And I like the path I took. I really do. Sometimes, it's all about chance. 'Charlie's Angels' was a chance.' Without that, I might have been living in Houston teaching ballet. When it came to my career, I took it day by day. I didn't have huge plans."
Jaclyn Smith, Farrah Fawcett and Kate Jackson are seen here on the set of "Charlie's Angels." (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
Smith married actor Dennis Cole in 1978 after about a year and a half of dating. They divorced in 1981.

"One day, I found a note in his pocket," Smith wrote. "The writer turned out to be a girl I knew. She was his son's girlfriend. I would not repeat the mistake I'd made with Roger. This time, I wasn't going to overlook what I learned, and I was not going to stick around and try to work it out. I didn't rationalize Dennis' actions, and I didn't blame myself. My one and only thought was to get out."
Actress Jaclyn Smith and her husband, actor Dennis Cole, are seen here on Feb. 22, 1980, at the Beverly Hills Hotel in Beverly Hills, California. (Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

In 1980, Smith met British cinematographer Anthony B. "Tony" Richmond while filming "Nightkill." They married in 1981. They welcomed a son, Gaston Anthony, in 1982, and a daughter, Spencer Margaret, in 1985. Smith wrote the marriage was strained by Richmond's struggles with alcohol and drugs.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Anthony B. Richmond and Jaclyn Smith attend an event at the White House in Washington, D.C., on Oct. 4, 1983. (Penske Media via Getty Images)

"I'd had enough," Smith wrote. ". . . I was done. I couldn't stay with a man who chose drugs and alcohol over his family. . . . We had a wonderful life when he was sober. . . . [But] I needed to do the best I could for my children, to protect them from the ravages I knew could come from substance abuse."
Fox News Digital reached out to Davis and Richmond for comment. Cole died in 2009 at age 69.
Jaclyn Smith's granddaughters: Bea, Olivia and Wren. "The joys of my life." (Courtesy of Jaclyn Smith)

"You know, in writing this book, I learned that I'm really strong," Smith said. "I had a great beginning. I had the best parents in the world, but I had marriages that didn't make it. Your heart gets broken here and there. You have successes along the way. And I worked hard to be there for my children more than anything. It's ferocious."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Jaclyn Smith arrives for the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards at the Peacock Theatre at LA Live in Los Angeles on Sept. 14, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)

"You have to give up control when you don't want to because you don't want anything to hurt them. I think of my journey, it's been unpredictable. I come away thinking, 'What would my parents think?' But I'm a girl who stuck to things, worked very hard and just gave it all to my family."

title: Sylvester Stallone reveals what he said to Trump after surprise Hollywood ambassador appointment
summary: Sylvester Stallone says he learned about Trump's Hollywood ambassador appointment while watching TV and later told the president it was impossible.
story: Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo brings ‘The Ingraham Angle’ to the red carpet at the Kennedy Center Honors and interviews stars in music and Hollywood.
Sylvester Stallone revealed that he was blindsided when President Donald Trump announced his appointment as a special ambassador to Hollywood.

Days before his second inauguration in January 2025, Trump shared a post on his platform Truth Social in which he named Stallone, Mel Gibson and Jon Voight as "Special Envoys," describing the role as a way for the three actors to serve as his "eyes and ears" in Hollywood and advise him on efforts to bring film and television production back to the U.S.
During a recent interview with The Sunday Times, the 80-year-old "Rocky" star recalled that he found out about the appointment while watching television.
SYLVESTER STALLONE'S 'TULSA KING' SEASON 4 TEASER SPARKS FAN FRENZY: 'THE KING IS BACK!'

"I was watching TV one night, and they go, ‘So Stallone and Mel Gibson and Jon Voight will be …’ And I went, ‘What?’ I said, ‘Excuse me? Really?’ Because if they had asked me in the beginning, I would have said, ‘This is not possible,'" Stallone said.

Sylvester Stallone revealed that he was blindsided when President Donald Trump announced him as a "special Hollywood ambassador." (Weiss Eubanks/NBCUniversal via Getty Images; Artur Widak/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Stallone told the outlet that he was hesitant about taking on the role because he didn't believe it was feasible. When asked if he had reservations after Trump's announcement, Stallone said, "Yes. Yes, because Hollywood, I guess it’s like feudal states."
'AMERICAN IDOL' DITCHES HOLLYWOOD FOR GEORGIA AFTER TWO DECADES AS CALIFORNIA LOSES ANOTHER PRODUCTION
"They have their little kingdoms," he continued. "You don’t go in and tell six studios how to do things. And Mel Gibson and Jon Voight, we’re kind of do-our-own-thing people. No, it won’t work."
The "Tulsa King" star recalled that he later explained his reasoning to Trump.
"I said thank you and ciao, because it’s impossible," Stallone said. "Hollywood works, and it will evolve."
"It’s corporate, and corporate people won’t want to hear me tell them about finance," he added.
Stallone said he told Trump that the role was "not possible." (Joe Raedle)
'I PLAY ROCKY' REVIVES THE GAMBLE THAT MADE SYLVESTER STALLONE A SUPERSTAR

In his original post on Jan. 16, 2025, Trump wrote, "It is my honor to announce Jon Voight, Mel Gibson, and Sylvester Stallone, to be Special Ambassadors to a great but very troubled place, Hollywood, California."

"They will serve as Special Envoys to me for the purpose of bringing Hollywood, which has lost much business over the last four years to Foreign Countries, BACK—BIGGER, BETTER, AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!" he continued. "These three very talented people will be my eyes and ears, and I will get done what they suggest. It will again be, like The United States of America itself, The Golden Age of Hollywood!"
DWAYNE 'THE ROCK' JOHNSON REJECTS HOLLYWOOD’S POLITICAL OBSESSION, BLASTS CELEBRITY ATTACK CULTURE
At the time, Gibson, 70, shared that he was caught off-guard by Trump's announcement and did not have previous knowledge about his presidential appointment.
Gibson said he was "surprised" by Trump's announcement.  (Mike Marsland/Mike Marsland/WireImage via Getty Images)

"I got the tweet at the same time as all of you and was just as surprised," he told Variety in January 2025. "Nevertheless, I heed the call. My duty as a citizen is to give any help and insight I can."
"Any chance the position comes with an Ambassador’s residence?" Gibson joked.

Though Stallone may not have been onboard with his role as a special Hollywood ambassador, the action star appears to have a friendly relationship with Trump and heaped praise on the president during a speech following his victory in the November 2024 election.
Days after the election, Stallone introduced Trump at the America First Policy Institute Gala held at the president-elect's Mar-A-Lago Club in Palm Beach, Florida.

"We’re in the presence of a really mythical character," Stallone said of Trump. "I love mythology. And this individual does not exist on this planet. Nobody in the world could have pulled off what he pulled off, so I’m in awe."

"When George Washington defended his country, he had no idea that he was gonna change the world," he added. "Because without him, you could imagine what the world would look like. Guess what? We got the second George Washington."
Stallone was later selected as a 2025 Kennedy Center honoree, with Trump personally naming him among that year’s recipients alongside George Strait, KISS, Gloria Gaynor and Michael Crawford.
Trump named Stallone as a 2025 Kennedy Center honoree. (Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images)

The actor has backed Republicans, including John McCain and Trump, but his political history has not been strictly partisan. Over the years, Stallone has made financial contributions to both political parties, donating to various Democratic candidates and committees, including former President Joe Biden and the Democratic National Committee, as well as Republican campaigns.

Meanwhile, Voight, who is a staunch supporter of Trump, appears to have embraced his role as a special ambassador. He has met with the White House and advocated for policies aimed at bringing film and TV production back to the U.S., especially a federal film tax incentive. Voight has been working with his manager Steven Paul and Paul’s associate Scott Karol as part of his push.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

After meeting with the trio at the end of last month, Trump threw his support behind a federal film and television production incentive, urging Congress to pass bipartisan legislation to "save" the American entertainment business.

In a Truth Social post on Aug. 31, Trump wrote that "Hollywood is a Complete and Total Disaster" and said there was "no incentive" for productions to stay there. He said meetings were being set up with leaders of both parties and urged Republicans and Democrats to "immediately craft Legislation to save the Movie, Television, and Entertainment Business in America."
Trump has a longtime friend in Voight, who he also appointed as a special ambassador to Hollywood.  (Mandel Ngan)
Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and U.S. Representative Laura Friedman (D-CA) later issued statements in which they voiced their support for Trump's proposal.

While speaking with the Hollywood Reporter earlier this month, Voight was asked whether Stallone and Gibson were involved with his efforts.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
They’ve been very busy, both of those guys actually have been extremely busy," Voight said.

However, Paul, who joined Voight for the interview, said, "Sly’s been doing his TV show, but Sly’s been very involved and he signed our letter."

title: Kid Rock calls Presley Gerber’s death a ‘tragedy’ as ex-girlfriend says he ‘deserved more time’

story: Presley Gerber, model and son of Cindy Crawford, has died at the age of 27. TMZ executive producer Michael Babcock discusses the investigation into Gerber's death and his past struggles with mental health and substance abuse.
Those who knew Presley Gerber best are sharing a personal glimpse at the man behind the famous family following his death.

PRESLEY GERBER, SON OF CINDY CRAWFORD AND RANDE GERBER, DEAD AT 27
Kid Rock and Presley Gerber's ex-girlfriend paid tribute to the 27-year-old model after his death was confirmed by his family. (Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images)

Charlotte D'Alessio pays tribute to ex Presley Gerber. (Instagram: Charlotte D'Alessio)

title: Princess Diana's brother Charles Spencer says King Charles 'gaslit' him over memoir claims
summary: Charles Spencer says he was "gaslit" by King Charles III after Buckingham Palace questioned his memory of a shocking post-Diana conversation.
story: King Charles confirms Prince Harry and Meghan Markle will not return to royal duties. A letter sent on behalf of the King explains their styles as His and Her Royal Highness remain in abeyance, and they are now akin to private citizens.

Princess Diana's brother, Earl Charles Spencer, fired back at Buckingham Palace after the royal household questioned his recollection of a conversation with King Charles III, saying he was being "gaslit" by the monarch.

Earlier this week, The Daily Mail published an excerpt of Spencer's upcoming memoir, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," in which the king's former brother-in-law described having a heated conversation with Charles after Diana's death. In the excerpt, Spencer alleged that Charles said, "We’ll forget her soon enough!," regarding his ex-wife during their exchange.

Buckingham Palace later responded to Spencer's claims, disputing the earl's account of the conversation and suggesting that grief may have affected his memory of events surrounding his sister's death.
KING CHARLES DRAWS ‘LINE IN THE SAND’ WITH PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE AFTER COUPLE CAUGHT OFF GUARD: EXPERT
During an interview with The Mail on Sunday, Spencer took issue with the palace's response.

"It is not every day you wake up to find you've been gaslit by the king," he said. "It was astonishingly provocative and below the belt because it was essentially trying to say I'd lied without the King being able to deny what I'd said."
Charles Spencer says King Charles III "gaslit" him in response to his claims about an alleged conversation they had after Princess Diana's death. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
"I also thought it was a rather poor imitation of the ‘recollections may vary’ quote, which was a much more elegant way of putting things, but in these circumstances entirely out of place," he added.
The remark referenced the palace's famous "recollections may vary" statement issued after Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's explosive 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey.
In the excerpt, published Wednesday, Spencer described a phone call he said he had with Charles six days after Diana died in August 1997.

"Prince Charles continued his stream of anger, without me interrupting. Then he stopped. I assumed the pause signaled an effort to bring himself under control, but then he unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death," Spencer alleged. "‘Rest assured,’ he hissed, ‘we’ll forget her soon enough!’"
PRINCESS DIANA'S HONEYMOON LETTER REVEALS A YOUNG BRIDE 'PLAYING WITH GROWN-UPS' IN THE ROYAL FAMILY
Diana died in August 1997 following a car crash in Paris. (Getty Images)

According to the excerpt, the king and the 9th Earl of Spencer disagreed over the decision to have Prince William and Harry, then 15 and 12, walk behind their mother's casket during the funeral procession.
KING CHARLES CONSIDERED QUEEN CAMILLA 'NON-NEGOTIABLE' AFTER PRINCESS DIANA, AUTHOR CLAIMS
A Buckingham Palace spokesperson issued a rare statement responding to Spencer's claims.

"While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss," the statement said, according to People.
Spencer stood by his account of the alleged conversation during an appearance on BBC One's "Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg."
When Kuenssberg pointed out that Buckingham Palace had denied his version of events, Spencer pushed back, saying, "But they haven't actually, Laura. They've sort of smudged that one, haven't they?"
Kuenssberg then read the palace's statement to Spencer, telling him that "the king is plainly furious."
"Well, is he furious? Is he furious or is he embarrassed?" Spencer asked. "Because I can tell you here and now, those are exactly the words he said."
Spencer alleged that Charles said, "We'll forget her soon enough." (Getty Images)
Spencer said he remembered the conversation clearly because he had spoken so infrequently with Charles, who was then Prince of Wales.
"I've only ever had two calls on the line with Prince Charles at any stage of my life," Spencer said. "I was hyper alert to what he was saying and those are precisely the words that he said."
Spencer said he repeated the alleged comment to close friends and family members immediately afterward "because it was so monstrous."

"Which, Charles, are the public meant to believe?" Kuenssberg asked. "Are they to believe you or are they to believe the king, the head of state of this country who's giving the impression very forcefully that this didn't happen? Who are we to believe?"
"Well, I'm telling the truth," Spencer replied.
"So, the king is giving an impression to the country that's not true. Misleading people, even lying?" Kuenssberg asked.

"I can hardly be responsible for what Buckingham Palace says," Spencer replied. "All I can tell you is what was said and what I heard and what shocked me. What else would have made me hang up on the king that day? It was something as outrageous as that slur against Diana."
When asked whether William and Harry would be upset by his account of the alleged phone call with their father, Spencer suggested his nephews were already familiar with his version of events.

"Well, I don't like to talk about what I've been speaking about to William and Harry, but this will not be a surprise to them," he said. "I will tell you that these words will not be a surprise to them."
A Buckingham Palace spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "We won’t be offering any comment."

Spencer said his dispute with Charles was due to the monarch's decision to have William and Harry walk behind their mother's coffin in the funeral procession. ((Photo by Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images))
Diana died at age 36 after suffering injuries sustained in a car accident in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel in Paris, France. Her partner, Dodi Fayed, and the driver, Henri Paul, also died in the crash.

Harry wrote about the decision to have him and his brother walk behind their mother's coffin in his 2023 memoir, "Spare," saying that "several adults were aghast" and that "mummy’s brother, Uncle Charles, raised hell," and that he told the royal family, "You can’t make these boys walk behind their mother’s coffin! title: Chad Gilbert, New Found Glory founding member and lead guitarist, dead at 45
summary: Chad Gilbert, founding member and lead guitarist for New Found Glory, has died at the age of 45. He had battled adrenal cancer since 2021.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Chad Gilbert, the founding member and lead guitarist for the punk rock band New Found Glory, has died. He was 45.

The band and the late musician's wife Lisa Cimorelli announced the news of Gilbert's death in a joint Instagram post Saturday. The post did not cite a cause of death, but Gilbert had battled adrenal cancer since 2021, and in February, underwent brain surgery after doctors found tumors.

"On the morning of September 20th, Chad Everett Gilbert passed away peacefully in his sleep," they wrote. "He left this world surrounded by friends and family and took his final breaths with his wife and mother by his side, just as he wished."
Chad Gilbert of New Found Glory has died at the age of 54.  (FilmMagic)
DUNCAN SHEIK, ‘BARELY BREATHING’ SINGER, DEAD AT 56

"We are devastated and shocked by how quickly he left us, yet so grateful for how peacefully and smoothly he went," they continued. "The amount of visitors that crowded the hospital lobby at a moment’s notice is a testament to how beloved and cherished Chad was, and always will be. He was a legendary musician, but his favorite accomplishment was being a husband and father. His biggest dreams came true. He is survived by his wife, Lisa, his daughter, Lily, his mother, Jackie, and his brother, Brian."

In their statement, New Found Glory, whose members include lead singer Jordan Pundik, bassist Ian Grushka and drummer Cyrus Bolooki, paid tribute to Gilbert’s lasting influence on the band and the deep personal bond that they shared.

"Chad’s guitar playing, songwriting, humor, and relentless drive helped shape New Found Glory for nearly three decades," they wrote. "Through more than a dozen albums, endless tours around the world, and more accolades than we ever could have imagined, Chad challenged all of us to grow as musicians, performers, and human beings."

"While we are devastated to lose him, we are so grateful for the incredible life he lived, the memories we shared, and the brotherhood we had. His influence will always be part of New Found Glory and his spirit will be felt on every stage we stand on, with every note we play."
The band's guitarist and founding member had battled adrenal cancer since 2021.  (Future Publishing via Getty Images)
'YOU'RE SO VAIN' SINGER CARLY SIMON SAYS PARKINSON'S AND CANCER DIAGNOSES KEPT HER FROM PUBLIC EYE
"Rest in peace, Chad. We love you forever," they concluded.
Fox News Digital has reached out to New Found Glory's management company Le Grand Music and label Pure Noise Records for comment.

Gilbert had been open about his battle with stage 4 adrenal cancer that was first diagnosed in 2021 and later spread to his spine, lungs and brain. He was initially diagnosed with metastatic pheochromocytoma, a rare adrenal gland cancer, in which the tumor grows inside the inner part of the adrenal gland.

In a February interview with People magazine, he shared that he began experiencing weakness on the left side of his body and difficulty walking while New Found Glory was promoting its latest album "Listen Up!"

After collapsing at home, Gilbert underwent a scan and doctors discovered he had three brain tumors, one of which required emergency surgery. Gilbert later underwent radiation and immunotherapy to treat the two remaining tumors.
After the operation, he told People magazine his diagnosis changed to adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC), which starts growing in the outer layer of the adrenal gland.
Gilbert helped form the Florida punk rock band in 1997.  (Redferns)
JOAN JETT CANCELS REMAINING 2026 CONCERTS AFTER UNDERGOING SURGERY FOR 'FRACTURED VERTEBRAE'
In a March Instagram post, Gilbert wrote that his "recovery has been bumpy at times," but that he was "feeling much better now and getting stronger by the day."

Gilbert returned to the stage in June, performing with New Found Glory during their tour stop in Nashville, Tennessee. He joined the band onstage to perform a few songs while using a mobility scooter.

"I got to play a show in front of my daughter, something I truly never thought I’d get to do again," he wrote in an Instagram post following the show. "And my beautiful wife and all the nurses and doctors, my amazing team that have kept me alive through my battle. It was very emotional getting up on stage with my band again to play. So many feelings all at once."

Gilbert shared daughter Lily, 5, with Cimorelli, whom he wed in 2020. The guitarist was previously married to Eisley singer Sherri DuPree. The two tied the knot in 2007 but split later that year. Gilbert was also married to Paramore lead singer Hayley Williams from 2016 to 2017.
New Found Glory made their breakthrough with their 2002 album "Sticks and Stones." (WireImage)

Born March 9, 1981 in Coral Springs, Florida, Gilbert helped form New Found Glory in 1997. The band broke through with its 2002 album, "Sticks and Stones," which featured the hit singles "My Friends Over You" and "Head On Collision" and reached No. 4 on the Billboard 200 chart.
New Found Glory followed up with 2004's "Catalyst," which peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard 200, and produced the singles "All Downhill from Here" and "Failure’s Not Flattering."

New Found Glory became one of the defining bands of the early-2000s pop-punk era. The band has released 12 studio albums and toured extensively around the world. Gilbert appeared on all of New Found Glory’s albums, including "Listen Up!," which came out in February.
In June, Gilbert returned to the stage for an emotional performance with New Found Glory in Nashville.  (Getty Images)

Outside New Found Glory, Gilbert was also known for his work in hardcore, including as a vocalist for Shai Hulud and with New Found Glory’s side project International Superheroes of Hardcore. Gilbert also worked as a producer for artists including A Day to Remember, H2O and State Champs, and collaborated with Fall Out Boy.

In addition to his wife and daughter, Gilbert is survived by his mother, Jackie and his brother, Brian.

title: Jack Osbourne admits raising kids without a nanny isn’t as gnarly as he expected

Jack Osbourne is opening up about the realities of raising five children, revealing that he and his wife, Aree Osbourne, have chosen to parent without a nanny.

"I’m a little more structured with my kids than my parents were with me," Jack previously told People magazine. "I won’t take them out of school just to go travel. We do a little bit, but I think structure is healthy."

summary: Frankie Muniz said the past six weeks have been a "nightmare" as he opened up about hitting rock bottom and doing the uncomfortable work ahead.
story: Bryan Cranston and Jane Kaczmarek told Fox News Digital that he made a $40,000 profit on a racecar and was getting into real estate while acting as a teenager on the show.
Frankie Muniz revealed he recently hit "rock bottom," describing the past six weeks as an emotional "nightmare."

summary: Dakota Johnson reveals she feels "a soul that wants to come through" as she opens up about hoping for motherhood before her "Verity" premiere.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Dakota Johnson thought her life would look a lot different than it does now.

"I really do. I do, but for whatever reason, that’s the plan of the universe," she said. "So I would love that. I hope that that happens for me. Johnson made a name for herself throughout the 2010s, starring in films such as "The Social Network" and "21 Jump Street," before landing the role of Anastasia Steele in "Fifty Shades of Grey," which became her breakout role.
She continued building her resume, starring in films such as "Peanut Butter Falcon," "Madame Web" and "The Materialists," but it looks like she plans on slowing down soon.

"I’ve worked back-to-back for so long that now I have this deep calling to shift my perspective a bit and maybe have a bit more of a real life," she said. "I’ve been gone for, like, 20 years. The people in my life are so used to me leaving for months at a time."

title: Christine Taylor’s ‘Hey Dude’ salary was far lower than castmates remembered
summary: Christine Taylor says her "Hey Dude" salary was just $3,500 per episode, far less than her castmates remembered earning on the Nickelodeon series.
story: The "Ned’s Declassified" alum explains why her tiny residual checks went viral and questions whether Hollywood needs a better system for penny payments. The former child star-turned lawyer is now the host of "Off My Meds."
Christine Taylor is looking back at her early Hollywood career — and revealing that her "Hey Dude" salary was far lower than her castmates remembered.

During an appearance on "The Secret World of Alex Mack" actress Natanya Ross’ "We’re Still Here, Babe" podcast Wednesday, Taylor — who played Melody Hanson on Nickelodeon’s Western comedy series from 1989 to 1991 — said she earned approximately $3,500 per episode by the show’s final season.
"By the time ‘Hey Dude’ ended, we had this discussion among our castmates, and everyone seemed to think [that] by the last season, we were making $5,000 an episode," Taylor said.
Christine Taylor opened up about her "Hey Dude" salary. (WireImage/Getty Images)
"No, we were making $3,500 an episode, I’m pretty sure, because they would bump us up $500 every season," she added.
Taylor said all of the cast members earned the same amount, despite her co-stars’ shared belief that they were making $5,000 per episode.
"Everyone in their brain was like, ‘$5,000.’ I was like, ‘No way, no way. That would have… no, it did not happen,’" she recalled.

The actress said she was careful with the money she earned while working on the popular children’s series. She also credited her family with helping her financially as she moved to Los Angeles and pursued acting.
JENNIE GARTH ADMITS ‘SCARY’ FINANCIAL SPIRAL AFTER ‘90210’ FAME
Taylor starred in "Hey Dude" in the late '80s. (Nickelodeon)
Taylor remembered budgeting closely, using laundromats and monitoring her spending during the early stages of her career.
The actress went on to appear in "Saved by the Bell," "Blossom" and "Robin Hood: Men in Tights" before landing her breakout role as Marcia Brady in "The Brady Bunch Movie."
‘BRADY BUNCH’ STAR SHARES THE SIMPLE WORD THAT SAVED HER FROM HOLLYWOOD TRAPS
Taylor also revealed that she was asked to lose 10 pounds before playing the iconic character in the 1995 film.
"Of course, I was embarrassed when that ask came my way," she said, adding that the request reflected the attitudes of the 1990s and "would never happen today."
FORMER DISNEY STAR DYLAN SPROUSE SAYS ACTING AS A KID WAS ‘CHILD LABOR’

Taylor later starred alongside her husband, Ben Stiller, in films, including "Zoolander" and "DodgeBall." The couple married in 2000, separated in 2017 and later reconciled. They share two children, Ella and Quinlin.

Ben Stiller and Christine Taylor share two children together. (Evan Agostini/AP)

Taylor’s experience is part of a broader pattern in Hollywood, where a recognizable television role does not always guarantee financial security. Several former television stars have revealed that their salaries and residual checks were dramatically different from what audiences assumed.
JODIE SWEETIN SHARES SHOCKING 'FULL HOUSE' RESIDUAL CHECK AMOUNT DESPITE SHOW'S MEGA SUCCESS

"The Sopranos" star Drea de Matteo recently said she was forced to find alternative income after acting work slowed down. The actress revealed that she turned to OnlyFans after facing financial difficulties and a lien on her home.

During an appearance on Jamie Kennedy’s podcast, de Matteo said she earned enough through the platform to pay off a $75,000 lien within 75 minutes of posting a bikini photo. She also said she sometimes earned approximately $100,000 per month.

Drea de Matteo opened up about her second source of income after acting slowed down. (Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images)
"I was not — people think I’m made of f---ing money," de Matteo said. "Everyone sees me coming, they’re like, ‘Here comes that rich b---- from ‘The Sopranos.’ And it’s like, no, I’m not at all."

More recently, "Married... with Children" star Ted McGinley revealed that he receives extremely small residual checks from some of his popular television projects, despite starring in long-running shows.

In an interview with Page Six, McGinley — who also found fame on "Happy Days" and "The Love Boat" throughout the 1970s, ’80s and '90s — said he's holding on to a "whole stack" of checks each worth a total of one penny.
Ted McGinley is seen in New York City on May 2, 2026. (Jason Howard/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images)
"I’ve been getting residuals all the time," said McGinley, who admitted the checks become smaller and smaller as the years go by.
