summary: Trump-backed U.S. Senate candidate U.S. Rep. Ashley Hinson asserted that the Iran "war needs to be brought to a successful and immediate end."
story: Iowa Republican Senate candidate Rep. Ashley Hinson, R-Iowa, discusses her highly competitive race against Democratic candidate Josh Turek and U.S. international trade policy on ‘The Story.’

As Americans endure elevated fuel costs with the midterm elections on the horizon, Rep. Ashley Hinson — a Republican running for U.S. Senate in Iowa — asserted in a post on X that the Iran war should "be brought to a successful and immediate end."

"Iowans are being squeezed and shouldn’t have to foot the bill at the pump or the checkout line for the war in Iran. We need to use every option at our disposal to provide some relief from high prices," Hinson said in the Monday post on X.

"That includes suspending the gas tax, pausing diesel exports, unleashing E-15 everywhere we can, reinstating the $1/gallon biodiesel tax credit, and creating a diesel relief program to help our farmers and truckers being crushed by the high costs," she continued.

These actions to lower costs are needed ASAP, and the war needs to be brought to a successful and immediate end," Hinson wrote.

title: China’s Xi set to arrive in Washington for high-stakes Trump summit as AI supremacy battle looms large
summary: China's President Xi Jinping arrives for a tense White House summit with Trump covering AI, tariffs, rare earth minerals and fentanyl exports.
story: Fox News’ Steve Harrigan reports on President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping’s expected talks on artificial intelligence at their upcoming summit on ‘Special Report.’
China's President Xi Jinping is set to arrive on U.S. soil later Wednesday for what is expected to be a tense showdown between President Donald Trump and the communist leader.

A red carpet rollout is planned for when Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, arrive at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday evening, replete with an arrival ceremony for the man who has found himself at odds with Trump on issues ranging from artificial intelligence and intellectual property theft, trade practices, rare-earth minerals to the communist country's support for Iran during America's military conflict there. Xi hasn't visited the nation's capital in more than a decade.

AI will be a major topic of discussion during the two-day summit, which officially begins Thursday morning and ends Friday evening, according to a senior administration official. Thursday will begin with a prestigious State Arrival Ceremony, including 479 military personnel from all branches on the South Lawn, State Floor and Rose Garden of the White House.
President Donald Trump shakes hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping while leaving after a visit to the Zhongnanhai Garden in Beijing, China, on Friday, May 15, 2026. (Evan Vucci/AP)
XI PREPARES CHINA ‘FOR BATTLE’ AS EXPERT WARNS OF GRAVE DANGER FACING US AHEAD OF DC SUMMIT

According to the official, a wide-ranging deal on possible tariff reductions on non-strategic goods is an expected topic of discussion, who also said the nation's leaders will discuss rare-earth exports and possible export controls. Trump is also expected to press China to do more to curb fentanyl precursor chemical exports.

Trump is also likely to press for the release of an American who has been wrongfully detained in China, Gulshan Abbas, who has languished in a Chinese prison for eight years. The country accused her of "participating in a terrorist organization" after her sister spoke out about China's genocide of Uyghurs, according to Forbes. House Speaker Mike Johnson and other Republicans have expressed confidence that Trump will push for her release.
EXCLUSIVE: FENTANYL DEATHS PLUNGE 22% AS TRUMP WHITE HOUSE TOUTS CRACKDOWN ON DEADLY DRUG CRISIS

President Donald Trump speaks with reporters before departing the White House for a trip to Beijing, to meet with China's President Xi Jinping, Tuesday, May 12, 2026, in Washington. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

First lady Melania Trump is expected to accompany Peng to the Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art, "to explore works spanning centuries of artistic achievement and Sino-American cultural exchange."
The day will end with an elaborate state dinner with high-profile guests, including many from the tech world.

Those guests will include Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, SpaceX founder and former Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) head Elon Musk, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser and Apple Board of Directors Chairman Tim Cook.

Trump boasted about American AI supremacy over China during an address to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York Tuesday, using his newly-minted term for the technology, "superintelligence."
TRUMP'S AI RACE WITH CHINA COULD BECOME THE BIGGEST MISTAKE OF OUR TIME
The Trump administration’s Gold Eagle program uses artificial intelligence to help uncover software flaws and coordinate security patches. (iStock; Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images)

"Every major new technology brings challenges, and superintelligence is no exception," said Trump. "Whoever wins superintelligence wins. That's the group that wins. And we're leading now over China by a lot and everyone else. And we're going to keep it that way."

Trump traveled to Beijing in May where he met with Xi, and the two sides agreed to a "constructive" trade truce, pausing a tit-for-tat tariff battle, but only for non-strategic goods. That deal has tentatively held, but during that visit, China also agreed to purchase billions more in American agricultural products like soybeans, and 200 Boeing aircraft. Boeing confirmed the order.

The 47th president said at the time that he struck "fantastic trade deals" that were "great for both countries."
Peter D'Abrosca is a politics reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Trump embraced a socialist he’s told voters to fear. Republicans aren’t thrilled
summary: Trump praised Zohran Mamdani weeks after calling Democrats "communists," leaving GOP strategists frustrated ahead of the critical midterm election.
story: 'The Five' panel discusses President Donald Trump's meeting with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani at Gracie Mansion, breaking down the key moments from their discussion, the issues addressed during the meeting and what it could mean for the relationship between the White House and New York City.

Six weeks before the midterms, President Donald Trump is complicating one of Republicans' central campaign arguments against Democrats — warmly praising New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani after repeatedly warning voters about the rise of socialism and communism on the left.

"I want him to be a great mayor, and he’s certainly got potential, got great potential," Trump told reporters as he patted Mamdani on the back after the two leaders met Monday at New York City's Gracie Mansion.
The meeting, where the two leaders discussed cost of living and housing issues, isn't sitting well with some Republicans fighting to keep control of the House and Senate in the midterms.

"All of it is self-inflicted, off-message, not helpful," a GOP strategist who asked to remain anonymous to speak freely told Fox News Digital. "None of these candidates out in these states, where these races are tighter and more competitive than they should be, are helped by any of this."
MAMDANI TELLS TRUMP BANNED NEWS OUTLETS ARE WELCOME AT NYC MEETING
President Donald Trump, left, and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani talk to reporters after meeting at Gracie Mansion, on Sept. 21, 2026.

Another Republican consultant, who also asked for anonymity, argued, "This is a president who is in a fully self-indulgent period. It doesn't seem like he really cares about winning. It's all off-key."
Less than two weeks ago, Trump told Republicans gathered in Dallas at the GOP's first-ever midterm convention that there is a "communist" takeover of the Democratic Party.

"In state after state, the Democrat establishment has been overthrown and replaced by crazed lunatics and radicals. They call themselves Democrat socialists, but actually, they’re communists," the president said.
THE GOP'S 'SOCIALIST' MIDTERM PLAYBOOK
United States President Donald Trump speaks during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly at United Nations headquarters, Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026. (AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura)
Fast-forward to Monday, and Trump held his third meeting with Mamdani since he won election last year as the first socialist and first Muslim mayor of the nation's most populous city.

A third GOP strategist, who was also granted anonymity, argued, "It seems he keeps on stepping on the message, making the election about how crazy the left is and communists and socialists and then appearing with them and yukking it up."
A top Trump supporter quickly took to social media to blast the encounter.

"I am a die hard Trump supporter and today I am feeling demoralized because Mamdani is a full blown communist jihadist. He is the spiritual leader of the communists in America and he met with the President today in NYC less than 45 days before the midterms," right-wing activist and MAGA champion Laura Loomer argued on social media.

Loomer, an internet personality who has carved out an influential unofficial role as a Trump confidant, emphasized, "How is this supposed to make Trump’s most loyal supporters feel? We don’t feel very happy today. We were told to FIGHT communism. But when we fight communism, we see the communist get rewarded... The base is very angry today."
DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB
President Donald Trump, right, and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani meet at Gracie Mansion in New York City, on Sept. 21, 2026. (New York City Mayor's office)

Alex Bruesewitz, a longtime Trump aide who now serves as a leading outside adviser to the president, shot back on X, writing, "I don’t understand the "Republicans" who are upset about the President having a friendly relationship with the Mayor of New York @ZohranKMamdani. It’s not wrong to have friendly relationships with people you disagree with. In fact, it’s healthy and good for you!"

Republicans are fighting against traditional political headwinds facing the party in power and a rough political climate fueled by persistent inflation, surging gas and diesel prices, what polls show is a very unpopular war with Iran, and Trump's underwater approval ratings.
To flip the script, a key part of the GOP playbook aims to turn what's normally a referendum on the party in power into a choice election by painting all Democrats on the ballot as far-left radicals.
While some Republican strategists say Trump is stepping on the message, others are not concerned.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
"I don't think it's that big a deal," veteran GOP consultant Dave Carney told Fox News Digital.
Carney said that Trump's meeting with Mamdani "goes with his role" as president, "and it's not a political role. The federal government and the president and the city have to work together."
But Carney, pointing to left-wing Democrats on the midterm ballot, said: "These other candidates out there who advocate these really radical crazy positions aren't elected yet."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Longtime Republican strategist and communicator Ryan Williams, referring to Trump, said the meeting "has the ability to make some on the right angry when he praises, Mamdani, but I don't think it has really has any political implications."
"Trump appreciates talent and whatever you think of Mayor Mamdani, the guy is politically talented," Williams added. "I think the president appreciates that."
Fox News reached out to the White House for comment, but didn't receive a response at the time this report was published.
Paul Steinhauser covers the national campaign trail from coast to coast for Fox News

title: Welder turned lawmaker sees a ‘nuclear bomb for work’ — and a chance to help blue collar Americans
summary: Rep. Riley Moore, a former welder, warns AI could be the "nuclear bomb" for blue-collar jobs or a force-multiplier for manufacturing workers.
story: Rep. Riley Moore, R-W.Va., tells Fox News Digital how AI could become a

Before AI threatened to reshape the kind of blue-collar work he once did, Rep. Riley Moore was a welder on an Appalachian mining operation. Now, as the technology races into the workplace, Moore argues it could make workers like him safer and more productive rather than replace them.

The West Virginia Republican has taken that message to the Teamsters and other labor stakeholders as Congress and businesses grapple with how quickly AI should reshape the workplace and how much of a role government should play amid economic and national security concerns.

"I started my career off as a welder and I come from a blue-collar background, not just myself, my mother's family [were] all welders, actually. AI represents a massive potential for positive advancements in manufacturing. But it also represents potentially the nuclear bomb for work as we know it in the world," Moore said in an exclusive interview Monday with Fox News Digital.

Representing a state still closely tied to mining and manufacturing, Moore has taken his message to the Teamsters and other labor stakeholders, arguing that AI should become a "force-multiplier" for workers rather than simply replace them.
WATCH: AMERICANS WARN AI WILL TAKE JOBS DESPITE REASSURING LABOR DATA: ‘JUST WAIT’

Volunteers hand out yard signs against a data center complex in Canaan Valley on June 30, 2025, after a public meeting organized by the West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection regarding an air quality permit application for a gas-fired power plant near Davis, W. Va. (ULYSSE BELLIER/AFP via Getty Images)

Moore said he leans toward finding the "positives" in AI development and that, if the technology can complement blue-collar labor rather than replace it, it could be a game-changer for the U.S. economy and its workers.

"I think AI certainly has the ability to extend the longevity of a worker in a particular trade. It can also make those jobs safer. It can extend the time period in which somebody can work without injury. And it can also create better efficiencies, which then can also better paying jobs here in this country."
I FEARED AI WOULD LEAVE MY COMMUNITY BEHIND. NOW I SEE A PATH TO PROSPERITY

"Or, it’s the nuclear weapon [against] work, it could potentially eliminate jobs as we know it and get rid of what is really critical, I think, to being a human being: which is human purpose, which work is certainly part of that and the dignity of work and contributing to civil society."

Moore’s district includes major commercial arteries like Interstates 79 and 81 and the new Trans-Allegheny U.S. 48, which the lawmaker helped open this year. The trucking industry, historically unionized, could benefit from AI, he said, while warning that self-driving rigs could endanger the trade.

"I'm against automated trucking, but I am in favor of having AI as part of trucking to make the road safer and keep that driver safer and make them more productive," he said, considering AI could act as a "co-pilot" to protect against drowsy driving or other dangers that come from being inherently human. The trucker would remain employed, and crash-prone 81 could become less so:
"That creates the types of efficiencies that we're looking for, certainly, but then also respects the dignity of the human being and the worker who is involved in it."

Religious leaders have expressed similar concerns about AI’s effect on the dignity of work. Pope Leo XIV’s May encyclical considered two biblical models for the AI era: "constructing the Tower of Babel" or following Nehemiah in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem.
"We certainly want to be Nehemiah," he said.

Moore has also spoken with and met with the Teamsters as unions grapple with AI’s potential effect on their workers. A Teamsters spokesperson declined additional comment but praised Moore’s appearance at the event.
Using AI to improve workflow efficiencies could raise wages, while U.S. leadership in AI could help counter China’s growing dominance in the AI "arms race."
FETTERMAN ALIGNS WITH TRUMP ON AI PUSH, WARNS CHINA BENEFITS FROM US 'OVERREACTION'

Rep. Riley Moore, R-W.V., speaks at a post-meeting press conference at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on January 14, 2025. (Photo by Bryan Dozier / Middle East Images / Middle East Images via AFP)
Data centers powering the technology have also become a point of controversy in Moore’s district and around the country.

In the Eastern Panhandle, within 100 miles of Washington, D.C., and in the high-elevation forests of Tucker County farther west, residents and local leaders continue to debate the arrival of data centers that have already begun proliferating farther east.
HOMEOWNERS IN THE HEART OF AMERICA’S AI BOOM ARE GETTING AN UNEXPECTED PAYOFF
As data centers expand across the country, communities are weighing new job opportunities against concerns over power, water and local impact. (Meta)

Moore said the three important questions are whether data centers will produce their own energy or rely on the local grid, whether they will siphon off public water or use "closed-circuit" cooling, and whether the community wants them there.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
A truck crosses into West Virginia from Pennsylvania along Interstate 79 in Monongalia County. Trucking is one of the industries that may be affected by the AI boom. (Charlie Creitz/Fox News)
Fierce debate continues over whether tax revenue from the centers can be balanced with community concerns.

"I think as a Republican, we certainly believe in federalism and allow those communities to be able to have input of whether they're going to have a data center in their backyard or not," he said.
Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

title: Zelenskyy to seek offramp for yearslong Russia war in UN speech after Trump reveals peace deal is close
summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy addresses the United Nations General Assembly with security proposals as Trump presses for a faster Russia Ukraine war deal.
story: Fox News correspondent Jeff Paul reports on escalating strikes between Russia and Ukraine ahead of a meeting between President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at the United Nations General Assembly. Paul details Ukrainian drone attacks on oil refineries in the Samara region alongside Russian strikes in Kyiv, Dnipro and Sumy.

NEW YORK — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is set to address the United Nations General Assembly Wednesday as President Donald Trump presses for an end to Russia’s war and Kyiv seeks to shape the emerging diplomatic push after more than four-and-a-half years of conflict.

Zelenskyy’s speech comes the day after he met with Trump in New York, where the two discussed finally putting an end to the war. Trump said that he believes a deal can be reached, though he did not disclose what that agreement would involve.
"We’re working very closely with the leaders of Russia and Ukraine, and we will get that one done," Trump said, adding that an agreement would happen "more quickly than people understand."
KUSHNER, WITKOFF SET FOR KYIV TALKS AFTER PUTIN MEETING IN US PUSH FOR PEACE

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is set to address the United Nations General Assembly Wednesday as President Donald Trump presses for an end to Russia’s war and Kyiv seeks to shape the emerging diplomatic push. (Al Drago/Reuters)

The Ukrainian president has said he is bringing "concrete security proposals and de-escalation measures" to New York for the annual United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) gathering. His government is also seeking additional air defenses, support for Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and help protecting food exports through the Black Sea.

The meeting with Trump came as Russia and Ukraine appeared to be weighing a possible pause in attacks on energy infrastructure. Zelenskyy has said Russian strikes on Ukraine’s energy sector, critical infrastructure and food exports should stop, followed by matching de-escalation steps from Kyiv.
UKRAINE SEEKS MORE US PATRIOT INTERCEPTORS AS BOMB SHELTER PROBE DEEPENS

Trump has also urged Ukraine to halt its strikes on Russian oil refineries. Ahead of his meeting with Zelenskyy, he called the campaign "a serious hit against the Russians," but added, "It’s also a serious hit on the price of diesel." In his U.N. address on Tuesday, Trump said he could use new tariff authority against buyers of Russian energy "if necessary" to bring the war to an end.
"This ridiculous and never-ending war with Ukraine must be ended. The whole world suffers as 25,000 people, mostly soldiers, are being killed each month. What a shame!" Trump said.
Zelenskyy’s speech comes one day after he met with Trump in New York to discuss proposals for ending the conflict. (Photo by Kay Nietfeld/Picture Alliance via Getty Images)

The competing priorities are likely to shape the diplomatic conversation around Zelenskyy’s Wednesday appearance before UNGA — Trump is pressing for a faster path to negotiations, while Ukraine is seeking the military support and security commitments it says are necessary for any agreement to hold.
The timing is especially consequential as winter approaches.

U.N. investigators have warned that renewed Russian attacks on Ukraine’s power grid could leave millions without electricity or heat. Kyiv is seeking more Patriot air defense systems, energy assistance and support for efforts to produce U.S.-designed interceptors inside Ukraine.
U.N. investigators have warned that renewed Russian attacks on Ukraine’s power grid could leave millions without electricity or heat. (Alexander KAZAKOV / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Zelenskyy’s remarks could offer a clearer indication of how Kyiv views the next phase of the war, including what it expects from Washington, how much responsibility it wants Europe to assume and what conditions it would attach to any cease-fire or peace agreement.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Ossoff challenged to return Epstein-linked donation or retract ‘Epstein class’ attack
summary: Democrat Sen. Jon Ossoff faces calls to return a $7,000 donation from Reid Hoffman, a billionaire who admitted visiting Jeffrey Epstein's island.
story: Georgia Republican Senate candidate Rep. Mike Collins issues a "demand" for Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., to return a donation from Reid Hoffman.

EXCLUSIVE: Democrat Sen. Jon Ossoff of Georgia is being criticized as a "hypocrite" and faces a challenge to return a sizable donation from a Jeffrey Epstein-linked billionaire or drop one of his main lines of attack on Republicans as representing the "Epstein class."

Ossoff has framed his re-election effort as pushing back on the influence of wealthy elites and getting big money out of politics. However, his campaign received the maximum legal contribution of $7,000 from Silicon Valley billionaire Reid Hoffman, a venture capitalist who previously admitted to visiting Epstein’s private island. Hoffman also donated $1 million to an Ossoff-linked political action committee, New Engagement PAC.

Hoffman has not been accused of any wrongdoing. But Ossoff’s Republican challenger, Rep. Mike Collins, says that accepting donations from Hoffman shows Ossoff "has been nothing but a hypocrite the entire time."

In an interview with Fox News Digital, Collins said he is giving Ossoff a very simple choice: return the Reid Hoffman donation or explain why the "Epstein class" does not include one of his own maximum-dollar donors.
DEM ‘EPSTEIN CLASS’ ATTACK BACKFIRES AS TOP CANDIDATES FUNDED BY EPSTEIN-TIED BILLIONAIRE

Billionaire Reid Hoffman (left), a known former associate of Jeffrey Epstein, made contributions to the campaign for Sen. Jon Ossoff (right), D-Ga., and to a PAC opposing Ossoff's challenger, Rep. Mike Collins, R-Ga. (David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images; Ben Hendren/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

On the campaign trail, Ossoff has railed against American politics for "running on secret money, corporate money, billionaire money" and accused the Trump administration of taking "American corruption to spectacular new heights." He released a statement earlier this year, saying, "We were told that MAGA was for working-class Americans. But this is a government of, by, and for the ultra-rich... this is the Epstein class, ruling our country. They are the elites they pretend to hate."

However, one of Ossoff’s donors, Hoffman, a Seattle-based billionaire, has previously admitted to spending a night on Epstein’s Caribbean island. Their first known meeting was on July 19, 2013, almost five years after Epstein pleaded guilty in Florida to state charges of soliciting prostitution and procuring a minor for prostitution. According to Massachusetts Institute of Technology records, Hoffman, then a member of the university’s Media Lab Advisory Council, met with Epstein alongside other faculty members on campus.

The next year, Hoffman visited Epstein’s private island, Little Saint James, and stayed overnight, The Wall Street Journal reported. Business Insider reported that in a recent podcast appearance, Hoffman admitted to staying one night at Epstein’s island as part of an MIT fundraising trip. Regarding his visit, he quipped, "Note to self: Google before going."
The Wall Street Journal reported that later in 2014, Hoffman sent Epstein ice cream, writing that it was for him or "for the girls."

Hoffman has since apologized for his association with Epstein, saying that "by agreeing to participate in any fundraising activity where Epstein was present, I helped to repair his reputation and perpetuate injustice. For this, I am deeply regretful."
DEMS DESCEND ON POSH ISLAND GETAWAY PACKED WITH DEEP-POCKETED DONORS AS MIDTERMS CLOSE IN

Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell attend de Grisogono Sponsors The 2005 Wall Street Concert Series Benefitting Wall Street Rising, with a Performance by Rod Stewart at Cipriani Wall Street on March 15, 2005, in New York City. (Joe Schildhorn/Patrick McMullan via Getty Images)
This election cycle, Hoffman donated $7,000 to Ossoff’s campaign.

In August, Hoffman also donated $1 million to New Engagement PAC, a Georgia-based political organization run by former Ossoff senior advisor Alexander Edelman. New Engagement has spent nearly $500,000 on media opposing Collins, according to September FEC filings reviewed by Fox News Digital.
Fox News Digital reached out to New Engagement PAC and Edelman for comment.
Collins told Fox News Digital that Ossoff’s acceptance of Hoffman’s donations is "sending a plain and clear message to the voters of Georgia."

"He doesn't care about our state; he doesn't represent the people of the state or the values of our state. If he did, he certainly wouldn't be associating himself with some of the Epstein friends out there, just taking money directly, maxed out, from Reid Hoffman who was in the Epstein files as an Epstein friend," he said.

He noted, "I could see it now if somebody gave you 20 bucks, and you didn't know who it was, but when somebody maxes out to your campaign directly, you know who they are, but yet you still take it. And then you turn around, and you go out there like a hypocrite, and you talk about President Trump and the Epstein files when you, in fact, are tied to it."
OBAMA STRATEGIST TURNS ON RISING DEM STAR OVER VIRAL TRUMP ATTACK: 'GRATUITOUS AND UNNECESSARY'
Rep. Mike Collins, R-Ga., leaves a meeting of the House Republican Conference at the Capitol Hill Club on Wednesday, December 4, 2024. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)
Collins argued that Ossoff, widely considered a rising star in the Democratic Party, is actually using his Georgia Senate campaign as a launching pad for a future presidential run.
"It's very clear that this guy is just using Georgia as a platform," he alleged. "He is going to get as much money as he can. He does not care where it comes from."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"So, we are here to condemn and demand that John Ossoff condemn Reid Hoffman, refund that donation, and tell Reid Hoffman we demand that you stop funding his campaign."
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
Fox News Digital reached out to Hoffman through Greylock, a venture-capital firm at which he currently sits as a partner. Fox News Digital also reached out to Ossoff's campaign for comment.
Peter Pinedo is a politics writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Mamdani fires back at Netanyahu, calls Israeli leader 'architect of horrific genocide' ahead of UN visit
summary: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani fired back at Benjamin Netanyahu's accusations of supporting Hamas by citing the ICC arrest warrant for alleged war crimes.
story: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani responded to criticism by Israeli President Benjamin Netanyahu by saying the world leader is "the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity."

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani fired back at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday after the Israeli leader accused him of supporting Hamas terrorists and inciting unrest against Jewish New Yorkers, escalating their long-running feud days before Netanyahu is expected in the city.
When asked by reporters about Netanyahu's video, Mamdani rejected the prime minister's accusations.

"We all know that what the prime minister has said in that video is not true," Mamdani said. "What we do know to actually be the truth when it comes to the prime minister is that he is the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity."
NETANYAHU ACCUSES MAMDANI OF 'FOMENTING HATE,' SAYS RHETORIC IS MAKING NEW YORK JEWS AFRAID

A split image shows Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, left, and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, right, who said on Fox News’ "The Story" that he would arrest Netanyahu if the Israeli leader visited the city. (Getty Images, Fox News)

The ICC issued the arrest warrant in November 2024 over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity, but Netanyahu and the Israeli government have rejected the allegations and challenged the court's actions.
Mamdani went further, leveling additional accusations against the Israeli leader days before he is slated to speak at the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

"And as the prime minister, he is the architect of horrific genocide against Palestinians," Mamdani asserted. "And just a few days ago, his military killed an 11-year-old boy in what is deemed to be a safe zone in Gaza. So that is what I have to say to his video."
ISRAELI UN ENVOY BLASTS MAMDANI AS 'CLOWN' OVER CALL TO ARREST NETANYAHU: 'IT'S A STUNT'
A split image shows New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, left, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, right. (Getty Images)
The mayor was responding to comments Netanyahu made earlier Tuesday in a video pledging to "tell the truth" about Mamdani when he speaks at the U.N.

"Shame on you, Mr. Mamdani. Shame on you for supporting the Hamas terrorist monsters who butchered our people. Shame on you for inciting riots against New York Jews," Netanyahu said in the video posted to X.
"I'm coming to the U.N. I am going to tell the truth about our heroic soldiers, and I'm going to tell you the truth about you," he added.
EXCLUSIVE: ISRAELI PRESIDENT HERZOG BLASTS MAMDANI, PRAISES TRUMP, SOUNDS ALARM ON IRAN

Zohran Mamdani speaks during a Wednesday interview on Fox News’ "The Story" with Martha MacCallum, where he discussed the Gaza ceasefire and said he would uphold an International Criminal Court warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. (Fox News)
The exchange is the latest chapter in an ongoing public feud between the two leaders and comes as Netanyahu prepares to visit the city Mamdani leads.

Earlier this year, Mamdani explored whether New York City could execute the ICC warrant against Netanyahu — an issue he had campaigned on — before acknowledging that the city could not enforce the warrant on its own.

Mamdani has previously called Netanyahu a "war criminal" and an "architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people." He also said over the summer that Netanyahu was "not welcome" in New York City.
"I want to be equally clear: Benjamin Netanyahu is not welcome in New York City, nor is any other war criminal at large," Mamdani said at the time.
Mamdani has also defended New Yorkers' right to protest during Netanyahu's visit, though he has said he is not encouraging them to demonstrate.
MAMDANI DODGES ON ‘POLITICAL THEATER’ OF EMPTY NETANYAHU ARREST THREAT, CALLS FOR US ACTION AND NYC PROTESTS
President Donald Trump meets with NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani inside Gracie Mansion on Monday, Sept. 21, 2026. (Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani @NYCMayor)
When asked in July what New Yorkers frustrated with Netanyahu should do when the Israeli leader visited the city, Mamdani pointed to protest as an option.

"One of the bedrocks of our city is protest," Mamdani said. "It is something that has been a part of what makes our city so special, that New Yorkers can express themselves whether they are in support or in opposition no matter on whatever topic."
More recently, Mamdani clarified that he had no plans to participate in protests surrounding Netanyahu's visit and said he had not encouraged New Yorkers to demonstrate.
"To New Yorkers, I have never encouraged them to protest," Mamdani said last week. "What I have always told them is that they have the right to do so in the city."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Following Mamdani's meeting with President Donald Trump on Monday, the mayor was also asked whether he discussed Netanyahu with the president.

Mamdani said their conversation remained focused on New York City and New Yorkers. The mayor's office said after Monday's meeting that Mamdani and Trump discussed issues affecting the city, including affordability and economic development.
"And when it comes to the prime minister, though, I've made very clear where I stand on that," Mamdani said.
Fox News Digital's Greg Norman-Diamond contributed to this report.
Michael Sinkewicz is a writer for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to michael.sinkewicz@fox.com

title: Florida AG accuses teacher of labeling student a 'misogynist' over 'conservative views': 'She should be fired'
summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier alleges a Pine View School teacher bullied a conservative eighth grader and labeled him a "misogynist."
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier alleged that a teacher harassed and attempted to "cancel" an eighth-grade student and labeled him a "misogynist" over what Uthmeier described as the student's conservative political views.

Uthmeier sent a letter to Sarasota County Schools' Superintendent Terry Connor and the school board over allegations that a Pine View School history teacher, Liz Ballard, singled out the eighth grade student on multiple occasions over his political views.
Ballard often brings up political topics during class despite the student telling her that his parents "expressly forbid" him from participating in the political discussions, according to the letter.
The parents' demand was ignored, and the teacher continued to hold political discussions, using the student as the "conservative perspective in the classroom," the attorney general said.
WASHINGTON FATHER SUES SCHOOL DISTRICT FOR DENYING RELIGIOUS OPT-OUT FOR 5TH GRADER FROM LGBTQ INSTRUCTION
A teacher allegedly harassed and attempted to "cancel" an eighth grade student and labeled him a "misogynist" over his conservative political beliefs. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

The teacher even labeled the student a "misogynist," spread that characterization around the school and "openly questioned the suitability and influence of the student's father," Uthmeier said in the letter.
Uthmeier's letter says multiple parents previously initiated HR investigations involving Ballard.
If the bullying and harassment allegations are true, Uthmeier said the teacher would have violated Florida law, School Board policy and basic ethical principles for educators.
"Ms. Ballard singled out this student and, in defiance of his parents' express instructions, pressured him to defend political positions on demand in front of his classmates," Uthmeier wrote.
PORTLAND PARENT BANNED FROM SCHOOL EVENTS AFTER OPPOSING GENDER IDENTITY ASSIGNMENT FILES LAWSUIT

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier said the teacher should be fired and never teach in Florida again if the allegations are true. (Joe Burbank/Orlando Sentinel/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

"She made disparaging remarks about his father. And by facilitating the spread of a damaging label throughout the school, she engaged in the reputational destruction of a child. Ms. Ballard's deliberate bullying and harassment of this eighth-grade student violated Florida law, School Board policy, and at least six ethical principles," he continued.
He said she should be dismissed from her role with the school district and her educator certificate should be revoked if the allegations turn out to be true.
"If true, she should be fired and never teach in Florida again," he said.
The attorney general gave the superintendent and school board an Oct. 1 deadline to update his office on the actions the district has taken or will take to address the allegations.
Connor said Sarasota County Schools received a letter from Uthmeier about allegations involving the teacher.
The attorney general said there have been multiple HR investigations involving the teacher initiated by parents. (iStock via Getty)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"We take the concerns seriously and will respond to the Attorney General's Office," Connor said in a statement to FOX 13. "Every student deserves a classroom where they feel safe, respected, and free to learn. No student should face harassment, humiliation, or retaliation because of their beliefs or their family's views. Respect for students and parents is fundamental to the trust our community places in our schools."

"The allegations in the letter warrant careful attention. We will examine the relevant facts and records, ensure a fair process for all involved, and take appropriate action based on the findings and requirements. To protect student privacy and the process's integrity, we will limit public discussion of individual details. This does not reduce our commitment to accountability. Our focus remains on our students' well-being, the professionalism of our classrooms, and the confidence families place in Sarasota County Schools," he added.

title: Harris keeps 2028 door open as she hits midterm campaign trail, warns ‘28 won’t matter’ without 2026
summary: Kamala Harris told Detroit voters she has not decided on a 2028 presidential run, stressing that the 2026 midterm elections must come first.
story: Former Vice President Kamala Harris addresses whether she is considering a 2028 presidential run during a fireside chat with NAACP leaders in Detroit on Tuesday. She says that her future goals depend on immediate political action, stating that '28 won't matter if we don't get through 26.'

Former Vice President Kamala Harris said Tuesday that she has not decided whether she will run for president again in 2028, telling voters in Detroit that the upcoming midterm elections must come first.
Harris was directly asked during a fireside chat whether she had thought about running for president in 2028 and whether another White House campaign was "on your plate."
"I have not decided if I'm going to run again," Harris said before turning the focus to the midterms.
"I do, I do sincerely believe 28 won't matter if we don't get through 26."
GAVIN NEWSOM SAYS HE WON'T RUN FOR PRESIDENT IN 2028 IF KAMALA HARRIS RUNS
Former Vice President Kamala Harris told voters Tuesday that she has not decided whether she will run for president again. (Bill Pugliano/Getty Images, File)
Harris said she was focused on traveling the country and reminding voters of the power of their voices ahead of the 2026 elections.
"And I'm a big believer that you can be. When you focus on the thing out there, you trip on the thing over here."

The exchange came during Harris' second event Tuesday in Detroit, where she participated in a fireside chat moderated by Rev. Dr. Wendell Anthony, president of the Detroit Branch NAACP and pastor of Fellowship Chapel, and Rev. Dr. Genetta Y. Hatcher, pastor of The Room Church.
Before asking Harris about a possible 2028 campaign, Anthony encouraged those in attendance to vote and referenced early and mail-in voting.
Harris was later presented with "take your souls to the polls" merchandise.
KAMALA HARRIS CLAIMS GOP 'CHEATING' AHEAD OF MIDTERMS, SAYS SHE'S FOCUSED ON STOPPING THE 'MADNESS'
Former Vice President Kamala Harris joins Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed for a roundtable discussion at Birth Detroit on Tuesday. (David Guralnick/Pool/Getty Images)

Earlier Tuesday, Harris campaigned alongside Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed at a roundtable focused on Black maternal health and healthcare costs. Harris used the event to criticize President Donald Trump's healthcare policies and voice support for El-Sayed.
Harris' remarks came as she focuses on the 2026 midterms while leaving open the possibility of another presidential campaign.
Harris became the Democratic presidential nominee in 2024 after then-President Joe Biden ended his re-election campaign.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
She went on to lose the presidential election to Trump.
Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

title: ‘Big Sister’ warning resurfaces as Massachusetts expands home visits after Clancy trial
summary: Anne Schlafly says Massachusetts' Welcome Family nurse home visits echo her mother Phyllis Schlafly's 1999 "Big Sister" government warnings.
story: Eagle Forum Chairman Anne Schlafly reacts to her mother Phyllis Schlafly's 1999 warning about government-backed home visits for new mothers as Massachusetts moves to expand its postpartum nurse program statewide.

Twenty-seven years before Massachusetts proposed to dramatically expand a taxpayer-funded program sending nurses into the homes of families with newborns, legendary conservative firebrand and grassroots women’s leader Phyllis Schlafly posed a question that her daughter says now sounds remarkably familiar.

"Are the American people willing to allow government agents to come into their homes to ‘advise’ them how to care for their babies?" Schlafly wrote in a March 1999 column titled, "Watch out for ‘Big Sister’ as Well as ‘Big Brother.’"

The warning resurfaced as Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey seeks $2 million to expand the state’s Welcome Family program, which offers nurse visits following childbirth. The program serves approximately 3,000 births annually, and the expansion is intended to make visits available following roughly 68,000 births statewide per year.
BLUE STATE GOV IGNITES ONLINE FIRESTORM WITH PLAN TO SEND GOV'T INTO HOMES OF NEWBORN BABIES: 'LUNATIC LIBS'

Stop ERA national Chairman Phyllis Schlafly leads members opposed to the Equal Rights Amendment in a song about pro-ERA forces planning a national demonstration in the capital city. The song stated, "You better look out, I'm telling you why, they're planning their trip, your votes to buy. Bella's bunch is coming to town." (Bettmann Archive)

The push comes in the aftermath of the Lindsay Clancy case, which put a searing spotlight on maternal mental illness. Clancy does not dispute that she killed her three young children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months — inside their Duxbury home in 2023.

Clancy's defense argued she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and was not criminally responsible, while prosecutors argued she knew her actions were wrong. The jury deadlocked, resulting in a mistrial.
For Anne Schlafly, chairman of Eagle Forum and Phyllis Schlafly’s daughter, her mother’s warning has now taken on new resonance.
"My mother was very prescient about the things that could happen if we let government intrude into our family lives," Schlafly told Fox News Digital.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TARGETS HEAD START BUREAUCRACY IN MOVE ADVOCATES SAY PUTS PARENTS IN THE DRIVER'S SEAT
President Ronald Reagan meets with American conservative activist Phyllis Schlafly in the White House Oval Office in Washington, D.C., March 21, 1983. (Universal History Archive/Univer)

"Her point was a government agent or an agent of the government has no business in your home, in your castle, snooping around and determining whether or not you’re raising the children the way the government wants you to raise the children," she said. "After all, the home is our castle."

Phyllis Schlafly’s 1999 column focused on Healthy Families America and similar home-visiting initiatives, warning about programs that screened families for risk factors, connected parents with health and social services and offered parenting guidance inside the home.
She also questioned whether programs officially described as "voluntary" would always operate that way in practice.

Massachusetts today describes Welcome Family as voluntary. Nurses assess the health of the "parents and caregivers" and newborn, answer questions about newborn care, screen for postpartum mental health concerns and connect families with additional services.
MICHIGAN LAWMAKER MOVES TO SHUT DOWN 'GUARDRAIL-FREE' CASH HANDOUT PROGRAM FOR NEW MOTHERS

Phyllis Schlafly of Alton, Ill., national chairman of STOP ERA, demonstrates in front of the White House Feb. 4, charging that President Carter was "using his wife" to promote the Equal Rights Amendment. (Bettmann Archive)

Notably, Massachusetts lists "ensuring that your home is safe" among the subjects Welcome Family nurses may advise parents about, though the program’s family information page does not specify particular home safety criteria.

The state has called Welcome Family an "entry point into the system of care" for families with newborns. Healthy Families America, the program at the center of Schlafly’s 1999 column, is also among the models Massachusetts lists within its broader Home Visiting Initiative, though it is separate from Welcome Family.
Healey described her vision for the expansion in broader terms during an interview on Boston Public Radio.

"Everybody in the state, when you have a baby, you’re going to have a home visit within days, weeks, and that will be an opportunity for a healthcare provider to make an assessment to see if you need some additional support and resources," Healey said.
FIERY VIEWS ON LINDSAY CLANCY AT WORK COULD GET YOU FIRED — AND BE PERFECTLY LEGAL, EMPLOYMENT LAWYER WARNS

Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey turns toward supporters after signing legislation strengthening abortion protections and prioritizing access to care at the Massachusetts State House Aug. 10, 2026, in Boston. (Jessica Rinaldi/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)
Anne Schlafly questioned what meaningful consent looks like shortly after childbirth.

"Is it really voluntary if you don’t have true informed consent?" Schlafly said. "If you have just given birth, you’ve been in labor, you’ve been under sedation, can you really recognize what you were signing up for supposedly on a voluntary basis?
"I think mothers need to have the full disclosure that this would be a government agent in the home."
The scale of the proposed expansion also concerns Schlafly.

"If government is going to expand their reach and hire a whole bunch of more people and use taxpayer money to send out all these agents to the families, I mean, that’s quite an expansion," she said. "This idea of coming in to inspect and see what’s going on in your home smacks of Big Sister and Big Brother both."
Massachusetts does not characterize the visits as inspections but as voluntary health and support services.

State officials point to results from the existing program. In 2025, Welcome Family offered 1,620 postpartum depression screenings, with 208 positive screenings. The state says every person who screened positively received a referral for services.
Schlafly said she does not object to families choosing to accept that help.
"If people want to have this help from Governor Healey, then they can avail themselves of it," she said.
Her dividing line, she said, is whether parents retain the ability to refuse.

"I think any time you make it compulsory, the line has been crossed," Schlafly said. "I would say the only way that this Massachusetts program could be acceptable is if the parents could opt out at any time."
Massachusetts’ published materials describe participation as voluntary.

Fox News Digital reached out to Healey’s office for comment and clarification about parents’ ability to decline visits, information collected during visits and whether information may be shared with other state agencies.
Nearly three decades after her mother warned about "Big Sister" entering the family home, Schlafly said she believes she knows what her mother would tell Massachusetts parents today.

"There’s no doubt that Phyllis Schlafly would advise parents to reject busybodies who want to inspect their home," she said. "The home is a sacred and private area, and Governor Healey has no business in the homes of Massachusetts parents.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Let’s leave her to the state house and not the kitchen table."

title: Kamala Harris says 'attack on DEI is an attack on maternal care' in appearance with El-Sayed
summary: Harris also accused political leaders who promote “family values" of hypocrisy while supporting policies she said could worsen the maternal health crisis.
story: ‘The Five’ co-hosts discuss former Vice President Kamala Harris campaigning for Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed.

Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday declared that an attack on diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) is an attack on maternal care as she joined Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed in Detroit to rally support ahead of the November midterm elections.
Harris made the remarks during a campaign roundtable with El-Sayed and several healthcare advocates focused on Black maternal health and healthcare costs.

"An attack on DEI, to recognize diversity, equity and inclusion, is an attack by definition on maternal care, including the need to protect Black women in connection with their pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum care," Harris said.
She noted that maternal mortality rates are disproportionately higher among minority groups, with the risk of death increasing up to four times for Black women and three times for Native women.
MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS LEADERS MUST ADDRESS ‘UNPAID DEBTS’ TO BLACK COMMUNITIES
"One in 12 women in America currently lives in a maternal care desert with limited or no access to maternal care," she added.

Harris then took aim at political leaders who tout "family values," arguing that efforts to end DEI programs strip away protections aimed at supporting certain communities during pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum care.
BIDEN-ERA DIRECTIVE FOR DIPLOMATS TO PEDDLE DEI ON FOREIGN GOVERNMENTS SCRAPPED BY STATE DEPARTMENT

"As one of the most — some would say the most financially strong economies in the world — we have the distinction of also having one of the highest rates of maternal mortality in the world," she said.
"So, it raises the issue of disparities and also hypocrisy when there are leaders who otherwise walk around every day talking about their family values."

Harris also turned her criticism toward President Donald Trump’s health care legislation, which she referred to as the "Big Bad Bill," arguing that it cut Medicaid spending with the support of former Rep. Mike Rogers, the Republican Senate nominee facing El-Sayed.
DR. OZ UNVEILS MEDICAID OVERHAUL, CLAMPS DOWN ON $2B FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS AND MANDATES WORK FOR ABLE-BODIED

"Medicaid is the largest funder for maternity care in America," she said. "Donald Trump cut Medicaid funding by a trillion dollars. These are the facts Mike Rogers supported that cut through that ‘Big Bad Bill.’"
Harris closed by reaffirming her support for El-Sayed in the Senate race, pointing to his position on maternal health and saying she believes he would be a "champion" on the issue.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"I'm here to support Doctor El Sayed, because, on this subject, I know he will be a champion," she said. "And I have a right to say that."
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: From Austin to New York, pro-China network fuels week of anti-US protests as Xi meets Trump
summary: Pro-China groups funded by tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham stage protests from Austin to New York, N.Y., as Trump prepares for Xi Jinping talks.
story: Fox News Digital senior investigations editor Asra Nomani discusses her team's investigation into far-left groups allegedly coordinating anti-ICE protests across the country, including the latest demonstrations in Austin, Texas. She breaks down the group's findings, the organizations involved and coordination behind the protests on 'America Reports.'

NEW YORK, N.Y. – As President Donald Trump readies for high-stakes negotiations with Chinese President Xi Jinping, a network of pro-China organizations funded by pro-communist tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham is taking to the streets from New York City to Austin, creating the image of rolling street unrest that lawmakers warn China can exploit to project a perception of chaos in the United States.

Yesterday, Singham’s wife, Jodie Evans, wore a trademark fuchsia straw hat and protested across the street from the United Nations on E. 47th Street, between First and Second Avenue, under an arch at Katharine Hepburn Garden, smiling widely next to agitators from the far-left CodePink nonprofit she co-founded and her American-born husband helped fund from his base in Shanghai. As part of their elaborate weeklong calendar, the activists railed against the U.S. military and its "all-out climate and environmental devastation." and then they marched to the offices of Open AI to demonstrate against data centers they allege "drive war" and "economic degradation."

The week’s protests reflect a pattern of rapid mobilization around breaking news and political flashpoints. The sequencing of events — combined with messaging sharply critical of the United States and silent about China’s human-rights, environmental and civil-liberties record — raises questions lawmakers debated last week about whether some activists function as "Trojan horses" for foreign adversaries such as China. Recently, Evans posted a video lauding China for building an economy that helps citizens "grow and thrive." Last year, Singham delivered a speech in China supporting the Chinese Communist Party and Xi's "new world order."
SOCIALIST, COMMUNIST GROUPS COORDINATE, PROMOTE ‘SPONTANEOUS’ ANTI-ICE PROTESTS IN AUSTIN

On Feb. 14, 2018, Jodie Evans, co-founder founder of CodePink, and Neville Roy Singham, founder of Thoughtworks, attend V20: The Red Party, a 20th anniversary celebration of V-Day and The Vagina Monologues, featuring a performance by playwright Eve Ensler and an after-party at Carnegie Hall in New York City. (Dave Kotinsky/Getty Images)

Lawmakers have warned that the cumulative visibility of such actions shape public perceptions, project an image of instability and give foreign adversaries a potential messaging – and negotiating – advantage as Trump prepares for high-stakes talks with Xi this week.

"The American people need to know that this is not just an organic movement," Rep. Jason Smith, R-Mo., chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee, told Fox News Digital. "There has to be more transparency across all areas with these kinds of activities."

Rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., chairman of the House Select Committee on China, told Fox News Digital the network’s grassroots image belies the serious funding infrastructure behind these groups. "In these situations where you have groups that portray themselves as grassroots, it's really more Astroturf, very fake," he said.
A split image of Chinese President Xi Xinping and President Donald Trump. (Maxim Shemetov-Pool/Getty Images; Artur Widak/Anadolu via Getty Images)
He said the protests "raises serious concerns" about malign foreign influence in the U.S., especially "when you see them actively speaking out against American interests."

The protests are publicly framed as separate events involving immigration, climate change, artificial intelligence, militarism and Israel. But their shared sponsorships show how organizations within the broader Singham network move quickly from one issue to another, using national organizations, local chapters, social-media promotion and shared venues to create a cumulative impression of coordinated street activism.

Moolenaar called for "clarification and transparency" regarding the organizations’ finances and questioned whether they should continue receiving tax-exempt status, adding that their political involvement may violate "campaign rules and political rules here in the United States."
LAWMAKERS RAISE ALARM OVER NEVILLE ROY SINGHAM'S $278M NETWORK SPREADING CCP PROPAGANDA IN THE U.S.
HASAN PIKER DEFENDS PRO-COMMUNIST, ANTI-ICE SINGHAM NETWORK ACTIVISTS AS 'WONDERFUL PEOPLE'

The significance of the week’s activity is heightened by the scale of Singham’s financial support for the network. A Fox News Digital investigation has documented how Singham has pumped $285 million through a donor-advised fund and shell companies into a broader network of six major nonprofits, media outlets and activist organizations that have promoted anti-American and pro-China messaging.

In that network, Singham has given CodePink $1.33 million, while doling out $22.44 million to the People’s Forum, a hub for the protest activity this week, and $1.098 million to BreakThrough BT Media, a media arm of the network that is flooding social media with images and videos from the coordinated protests this week.

As Fox News Digital reported exclusively, the Justice Department’s Southern District of New York has convened a federal grand jury investigation into Singham’s financial network, sources say. Prosecutors are examining whether Singham, the organizations he funded or their leaders engaged in alleged wire fraud, bank fraud or money laundering, according to sources. Singham hasn’t been charged with a crime, and the investigation doesn’t establish that he personally directed each protest. Singham, the People's Forum, CodePink and BreakThrough News haven't responded to repeated requests for comment.

The sequence began Sunday night in Austin, where socialist and communist organizations rapidly promoted an anti-ICE protest after the shooting of Venezuelan national Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez. The Democratic Socialists of America, Freedom Road Socialist Organization and Party for Socialism and Liberation amplified calls for demonstrators to gather at 8121 Research Blvd. in Austin.

Although media accounts described the protest as organic, the mobilization moved through an existing national activist infrastructure. The Singham network's Party for Socialism and Liberation and the Freedom Road Socialist Organization circulated video and protest messaging, while Democratic Socialists of America promoted the gathering as "spontaneous" and called supporters to the streets. The protest later spread beyond Austin, with activists in Pearsall, Tex., pledging to put "boots on the ground."

In response to Fox News Digital’s reporting on the protests, the Party for Socialism and Liberation published a video with an activist "rejecting" criticism of its Austin protests as a "nefarious" coordinated event and called the protests the result of "righteous anger."
The Party for Socialism and Liberation, Democratic Socialists of America and Freedom Road Socialist Organization didn't respond to requests for comment.

On June 4, 2024, CodePink's Medea Benjamin interrupts a Capitol Hill news conference in Washington, D.C., organized to commemorate the anniversary of the 1989 Tiananmen Square Massacre and to discuss the "ongoing struggle for human rights and democracy in China." Her sign says, "China is not our enemy." (Nathan Posner/Anadolu via Getty Images)
CHINESE PROPAGANDA, SINGHAM NETWORK, FOREIGN DARK MONEY LINKED TO CAMPAIGNS AGAINST DATA CENTERS

On Monday, the network’s actions moved to New York City, where Singham’s wife, Evans, and her cadre of CodePink activists began a week of demonstrations tied to Climate Week and the United Nations. CodePink co-founder Susan Medea Benjamin has led previous protests, including demonstrations supporting China.

After the environmental activism led by Evans outside the UN, CodePink agitators joined an "Unplug OpenAI" protest outside OpenAI’s offices on Lafayette Street, linking artificial-intelligence data centers to the "military-industrial complex." The group’s weeklong schedule promised "disruptions" and "bird-dogging," a tactic in which seemingly regular people plant themselves in restaurants, conferences and other events to heckle and harass public officials and even ordinary citizens, peppering them with questions and shaming rhetoric without any real interest in a dialogue.

Early Tuesday, CodePink celebrated its "fearless cofounder" Evan’s birthday with an Instagram collage of photos from her decades of activism, including the image of a smiling Evans in her pink straw hat, standing beside fuchsia balloons from a campaign called "China Is Not Our Enemy" that the group launched after receiving the donations from Singham. Another photo included her beaming smile next to controversial Marxist influencer Hasan Piker, as the two joined a caravan to support the Communist Party of Cuba.

Later in the day, CodePink activists moved their campaign inside the People’s Forum, a Manhattan hub for communist organizing for a screening of a film, "Earth’s Greatest Enemy," by a fiercely anti-U.S. film company, Watermelon Pictures, chronicling the U.S. military as "one of the most significant drivers of environmental destruction," the "world’s largest institutional polluter."

Back in Austin, a short while later at about 5:30 p.m. Eastern Time, the Singham network's BreakThrough News propaganda network posted edited video clips from the Austin protests, headlined: "SECOND DAY OF PROTESTS IN AUSTIN AFTER ICE SHOOTS VENEZUELAN DELIVERY DRIVER."
For Wednesday, Evans and CodePink promise more protests against the U.S. military's "role in climate issues."

On Thursday, as Xi meets with Trump in the White House, the People’s Forum, CodePink, the Palestinian Youth Movement and other groups in the Singham network are hitting the streets to protest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. In social media posts, the groups are advertising a Thursday march from Bryant Park to the United Nations, calling on New Yorkers to "reject war criminal Benjamin Netanyahu and the genocidal Zionist project."

That day, Evans and CodePink also plans to participate in a teach-in on "War & Climate: What U.S. Imperialism Demands of Our Climate Justice Movements" before joining the anti-Israel agitation. Organizers are lashing out against the "genocide" in Gaza and blasting "ecocide."

By Friday, as Xi readies to leave town, the protests will go full circle back to Austin, with the Singham network’s Party for Socialism and Liberation planning a protest at 6 p.m. at City Hall with the simple message: "Now is the time for us all to be brave, to follow the example of Minneapolis earlier this year, and TAKE TO THE STREETS!"
