title: Fox News AI Newsletter: Trump shreds AI doomer 'hoax'
summary: The Fox News AI Newsletter covers the latest artificial intelligence technology advancements, including the challenges and opportunities AI presents now and for the future.
story: 'Outnumbered' panel analyze requests from Anthropic and OpenAI executives for federal artificial intelligence regulation ahead of the midterm elections. They react to President Donald Trump's dismissal of doomsday scenarios and White House tech advisor David Sacks' opposition to development pauses.
IN TODAY'S NEWSLETTER:
- Trump calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during summit, dismisses AI fears as 'hoax'
- Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz's 'effective altruism' network tied to AI regulation push
- Sam Altman says OpenAI's won't go public in 2026 amid AI safety concerns

FUTURE ON THE LINE: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang received a surprise phone call from President Donald Trump on Monday, in which the president dismissed fears that AI poses an existential threat to humanity and argued against calls to slow frontier AI development.

LISTING LIMBO: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman signaled that the company will delay its initial public offering (IPO) amid concerns about the safety and alignment of AI models given potential risks they could pose to society.

DIGITAL GUARDRAILS: Microsoft on Monday revealed a draft of a new "Humanist AI Code of Conduct" that outlines the principles that will govern its development of AI models in an effort to get feedback ahead of publishing a revised version later this year.

STEP FORWARD: Researchers are now using artificial intelligence to help tailor cancer treatments and uncover overlooked uses for existing medicines. Other systems can search microscopic images or identify subtle biological signals that people could easily miss.

OPINION: Every morning brings a new warning about "artificial intelligence" (AI) along the lines of, "We are all going to die." By afternoon, or by the next day at the latest, comes the counter-warning: "Stand down. Nothing to see here."
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman speaks during the Federal Reserve's Integrated Review of the Capital Framework for Large Banks Conference in Washington, D.C., July 22, 2025. (REUTERS/Ken Cedeno)
PLAYING SAFE: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman outlined two scenarios that he sees could derail progress in developing artificial intelligence (AI) and must be avoided.

OPINION: The cat is out of the bag. Simmering concerns about AI agents going rogue, plotting against their owners and hacking outside companies, and new systems coming perilously close to being uncontrollable by humans, are boiling over. Industry insiders warning that AI bots might kill us all are stoking our worst nightmares.

ZONING WARS: Democratic lawmakers are calling for tighter restrictions on data centers, while Republicans say the facilities could boost the economy and keep the U.S. ahead in the artificial intelligence (AI) race.

DOOM FOR DOLLARS: Concerns about artificial intelligence spelling doom for the human race are being linked to a "cult-like" philanthropy movement known as "effective altruism" supported by billionaire Democratic megadonor and Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz, according to a policy analyst.

SOURCING SOLUTION: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Tuesday told lawmakers in Congress that the U.S. needs to foster open artificial intelligence (AI) models to compete with those made by Chinese firms.
An Amazon Web Services data center in Stone Ridge, Virginia, on Sunday, July 28, 2024. (Nathan Howard/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

'DOOM' AND BOOM: "Doomer"-driven AI regulation could kneecap the U.S. against China while helping tech giants lock in their lead over smaller startups, a former Pentagon AI official who also worked for AI company Palantir Technologies told Fox News Digital.

WAKE-UP CALL: Former President Barack Obama urged Democrats during a private fundraiser in New York City Thursday to place artificial intelligence near the center of their political agenda ahead of the midterms and 2028 presidential race while warning that the technology could become dangerous without greater oversight as voters increasingly raise concerns about jobs, privacy and data centers.

GUARDRAIL DEBATE: House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., rejected an emergency moratorium on artificial intelligence development Sunday during CNN's "State of the Union," warning that slowing American innovation could allow China to pull ahead as tech executives and lawmakers intensify calls for new AI safety measures.

NUCLEAR ECHOES: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Sunday compared the U.S.-China artificial intelligence (AI) race to the Cold War with the Soviet Union, warning both nations must manage the threat of "potential destruction" from each other.

title: Driverless racing goes global. Will fans care?
summary: Autonomous race cars hit Laguna Seca and Imola Circuit at speeds topping 157 mph, but the Abu Dhabi Autonomous Racing League faces a fan problem.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Autonomous race cars are starting to show up on some very famous tracks. On Sept. 3, the Indy Autonomous Challenge brought its driverless race cars to WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca in California. Purdue AI Racing set a new autonomous track record and finished second in a head-to-head passing competition. Italy's Unimore Racing took the win.

Two days later, autonomous racing took another step forward in Europe. Five teams brought fully autonomous race cars to Italy's Imola Circuit for the Abu Dhabi Autonomous Racing League's first race outside Abu Dhabi. Team Kinetiz came from fourth on the grid to win the 12-lap event.
Now autonomous racing has reached major circuits in the U.S., Europe and Abu Dhabi. The technology clearly travels. The bigger question is whether the fans will follow.

NEW! Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better Healthcare With AI In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you take a more active role in your healthcare. You’ll learn how to organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare questions for your next doctor’s visit. No technical experience is needed.
Register for free now at CyberGuyLive.com.
WAYMO RECALLS ROBOTAXIS OVER CONSTRUCTION-ZONE RISK
University teams and their autonomous race cars gather at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca after the Indy Autonomous Challenge’s Sept. 3, 2026 competition. (Indy Autonomous Challenge)
Driverless racing is becoming a global competition

The races at Laguna Seca and Imola came from two different autonomous racing programs. The Indy Autonomous Challenge brings together university teams that develop AI drivers for identical race cars. At Laguna Seca, nine university teams from North America, Europe and Asia were scheduled to compete.

The Sept. 3 event pushed the competition further by adapting the Indy Autonomous Challenge's passing format to a road course for the first time. Instead of several cars racing as a pack, two autonomous cars take turns in attacking and defending roles. The software has to manage spacing and decide when it can safely make a move.

Purdue became the only American team to qualify for that portion of the competition. Its car also set a 1:27.731 autonomous lap record before finishing runner-up to Unimore. Then came Imola. A2RL brought autonomous racing from its home at Yas Marina Circuit in Abu Dhabi to Europe for the first time. The league says Imola represents another step toward its goal of creating an international championship for fully autonomous race cars.
Five autonomous race cars headed to the grid at Imola

Imola raised the difficulty again. Kinetiz, Constructor Racing, PoliMOVE, Unimore Racing and two-time A2RL champion TUM entered the event. Each team competed with identical EAV-25 race car hardware based on the Dallara Super Formula SF23 platform. That means much of the competitive advantage came from the software each team developed.
The AI had to figure out where the car was, understand what was happening around it and decide what to do next. Then it had to turn those decisions into braking and steering inputs at racing speed.

TUM ran into a technical problem on the formation lap and returned to the pits before the rolling start. That left the remaining cars to fight for position. Unimore had started from pole and led the race. Then things went wrong.
WAYMO VEHICLES 'PUTTING AMERICAN LIVES AT RISK,' SOURCE WARNS AMID AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE COMPANY'S MASSIVE RECALL
Team Kinetiz celebrates with its autonomous race car after winning Europe’s first multi-car autonomous race at Italy’s Imola Circuit on Sept. 5, 2026. (A2RL)
A crash showed how hard autonomous racing can be

Unimore set the fastest lap of the race before suffering a technical problem that caused the car to slow dramatically. PoliMOVE was close behind and hit the slowing Unimore car from the rear. The collision ended both teams' runs. That opened the door for Kinetiz.

The Singapore-UAE team had started fourth but moved into the lead and won by 10.963 seconds over Germany's Constructor Racing. PoliMOVE was classified third. The crash may also be one of the most revealing parts of the race.

Driving fast on an empty track is one challenge. Reacting when the car directly in front of you suddenly loses speed creates a much harder problem. That is exactly the type of unpredictability autonomous systems have to learn to handle.
These AI race cars are getting seriously fast

These cars are moving a lot faster than you might expect. At Imola, PoliMOVE hit about 157 mph with nobody behind the wheel. During testing, the fastest autonomous lap came within 0.85 seconds of a benchmark lap set by Super Formula driver Juju Noda. That is surprisingly close.

In Abu Dhabi last year, former Formula 1 driver Daniil Kvyat still set a faster lap than the autonomous challenger, but the gap had narrowed to just 1.58 seconds. So the question has changed. We already know these cars can get around a racetrack at serious speeds. Now we are seeing what happens when they have to race another car and make those decisions in real time.
But who are fans supposed to root for?

Here's where autonomous racing faces a challenge that has nothing to do with speed. Part of the fun of racing is having someone to root for. Fans follow drivers, get to know their personalities and pick favorites. Take the driver out of the car and suddenly that connection looks very different.

With autonomous racing, you are rooting for the team behind the software. For some tech fans, that may be enough. Watching engineers figure out how to make an AI-powered race car faster and smarter could become part of the appeal. But will people come back race after race?

We are already starting to get a sense of that. The Indy Autonomous Challenge returned to Laguna Seca this year and moved from solo time trials in 2025 to head-to-head passing on the road course. Just two days later, five autonomous race cars competed together at Imola in Italy.
Now the harder part may be building the kind of connection that keeps people watching after the surprise of seeing an empty cockpit wears off.
Five fully autonomous race cars compete at Italy’s Imola Circuit during A2RL’s first international race on Sept. 5, 2026. (A2RL)
So what is the point of racing cars without drivers?

There is another reason these competitions are worth watching. Racetracks give autonomous driving researchers a place to push software extremely hard. At Laguna Seca, Purdue's team spent weeks practicing and used simulation to find bugs in its software before race day. At Imola, the AI had to deal with high speeds and other autonomous cars making their own decisions.

That pressure can reveal weaknesses quickly. A passenger car on a public road faces a very different environment. It has to deal with pedestrians, intersections and countless situations that do not exist on a closed racetrack.

So winning an autonomous race does not mean the same software is ready to drive you around town. Still, the basic challenge overlaps. An autonomous vehicle has to understand what is happening around it and decide how to respond. Racing forces researchers to test those capabilities at the edge of what the vehicle can handle. That is where this becomes relevant even if you never watch a single autonomous race.
Kurt's key takeaways

Here's what gets me about autonomous racing. We have gone from asking whether AI can keep a race car on the track to watching these cars chase each other at more than 150 mph. That is pretty remarkable. But speed alone will not turn this into a sport people care about. Part of what makes racing so compelling is the person inside the car. You follow the driver, learn their personality and pick someone you want to win. When the cockpit is empty, that connection changes completely. Could fans eventually start rooting for the teams behind the technology instead? I can see Purdue students and engineers developing their own following as these competitions grow. But autonomous racing still has to prove that watching great software compete can be as exciting as watching a great driver push a car to the limit. The cars are clearly ready to race. Now we get to see whether the fans are ready to care.
Would you watch an entire race with nobody behind the wheel? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com.

title: Texas lawmaker warns accused wife-killer's Italy escape could open 'Pandora's box' for future suspects
summary: Lee Gilley fled Texas for Italy after being charged with capital murder, and a lawmaker warns the extradition fight could set a dangerous precedent.
story: Texas state Rep. Brian Harrison tells Fox News Digital he fears foreign courts could gain sway over how criminals are punished after an accused wife-killer fled to Italy and forced the death penalty off the table.

One Texas lawmaker is warning that an accused wife-killer's escape to Italy, which forced prosecutors to remove the death penalty as a possible sentence, could open a "Pandora's box" for future criminals.

Lee Gilley, 39, has been charged with capital murder in the October 2024 death of his wife, Christa, who was nine weeks pregnant at the time of her death. The Harris County Medical Examiner's office ruled her death a homicide caused by neck compression. Gilley has entered a not guilty plea.

According to authorities, Gilley cut off his ankle monitor on May 1 and fled Texas before his trial was set to begin. Court records indicate he traveled to Milan Malpensa Airport in Italy under a false identity and with forged travel documents. Italian authorities subsequently took him into custody.
TEXAS MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING PREGNANT WIFE ALLEGEDLY CUTS OFF ANKLE MONITOR AND FLEES TO ITALY
Prosecutors allege Lee Mongerson Gilley killed his wife, Christa Bauer Gilley, who was nine weeks pregnant, in Houston in 2024. (Christa Bauer Gilley/Facebook)

Dick DeGuerin, Gilley's U.S. attorney, previously told Fox News Digital that Italian judges required a written guarantee that prosecutors would not pursue the death penalty before they would consider returning him. He said Italian authorities may also seek assurances that Gilley would not face a sentence of life without parole.

"Most civilized countries in the free world have abolished the death penalty," he told Fox News Digital on Tuesday. "The U.S. and Texas should do the same, in my opinion, after spending 61 years of my adult life in the criminal justice system."

The Harris County District Attorney's Office announced in direct response to the Italian judges that it won't be pursuing the death penalty against Gilley, but stopped short of pledging not to pursue life without parole, noting that he could be eligible for commutation.
TEXAS MAN ACCUSED IN PREGNANT WIFE'S MURDER FIGHTS TO REMAIN IN ITALY, CITING 'LIFESTYLE AND CULTURE'
Texas State Representative Brian Harrison told Fox News Digital he's very concerned about the prospect of a European country controlling how criminals are sentenced in his state.

"You're almost opening Pandora's box in sort of a roundabout way, allowing ... some of those European socialist soft on crime liberal politicians to be able to wield influence over what happens in Texas courts," Harrison said. "I do not want foreign governments, foreign officials, foreign courts having anything to do with how we enforce criminal laws here in the state of Texas."
"What's to stop them from moving the goalposts even further?"
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
Lee Mongerson Gilley, 39, is accused of murdering his wife, Christa Bauer Gilley, and their unborn child in Houston in 2024, according to KPRC. (Christa Bauer Gilley/Facebook)
He also said this could create a horrible precedent for future suspects who may want to find creative ways to reduce their potential sentence.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

"If you can somehow, once you're out on bond, just touch foot on foreign soil and then turn the extradition hearings into basically a way to whittle down potential punishments ... the implications are profound and very concerning to me," Harrison said.
SEND US A TIP
A hearing was held before the Turin Court of Appeal on Sept. 7. DeGuerin told Fox News Digital that Gilley's extradition was again delayed.

He is charged with capital murder in the death of his wife, Christa Gilley. (Melissa Phillip/Houston Chronicle via Getty Images)

During a July 15 hearing at the Turin Court of Appeal, Gilley said he is seeking protection in Italy, according to NBC News. The Turin Court of Appeal blocked the extradition request during a hearing on July 20.

Gilley's Italian attorney, Monica Grosso, previously said Christa had a blood disorder and that blood discovered in the couple's bedroom did not align with the prosecution's version of how she died.

Defense attorney Ed McClees and his client, Lee Mongerson Gilley, appear in the 497th District Court at the Harris County Justice Center in Houston on Oct. 17, 2024. Gilley is charged with capital murder in the death of his wife, Christa Gilley. (Melissa Phillip/Houston Chronicle via Getty Images)
"I am seeking protection in Italy," Gilley said. "They want to punish me, and I am asking for protection for myself and my children."

title: Massachusetts lesbian bar ignites fury after easing mask rules for one night a week
summary: Last Ditch Bar in Greenfield, Massachusetts, faces a boycott and accusations of ableism after lifting its mask mandate on Saturdays to stay afloat.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A lesbian bar in Greenfield, Massachusetts, sparked community backlash after lifting its mask mandate for one night a week, with accusations of ableism and boycott directed at the struggling business.

Last Ditch Bar and Arts Venue recently removed its mask requirement on Saturdays in an effort to boost business, but some members of the small city's queer community objected to the change, according to The Boston Globe.

Some critics accused the bar's owners of putting disabled people at risk and compared the policy change to a "mass disabling event" and a "eugenicist" attack while also wishing violence against the establishment, according to The Boston Globe.

"I hope your venue gets firebombed for robbing my fellow immunocompromised people of their Saturday plans just to scrape extra revenue from ablists [sic]," one commenter wrote on the bar's social media post announcing the change.
IDAHO COFFEE SHOP OWNER DEFENDS EJECTING PRO-LIFE GROUP FROM HIS BUSINESS AFTER BACKLASH
A lesbian bar in Greenfield, Massachusetts, sparked community backlash after lifting its mask mandate for one night a week. (Google Maps)
"People like you kill disabled people in the name of your own leisure and convenience," wrote another.
"Just say you’re being complicit in a mass disabling event and get it over with," a third said.
"When y'all close, let the record state it was ableism + complying in advance, because that's what it is," another wrote.
"Does COVlD not disable people on Saturday nights?" added another user, who had a picture of himself in a mask as his profile picture.

This comes years after the COVID-19 pandemic was declared over by the federal government in 2023. State and local governments, as well as most businesses across the country, had also lifted masking requirements several years ago.
Additionally, Greenfield had not reported a COVID-19 case in more than two months, according to The Boston Globe.
The bar has been sparsely attended on what would normally be busy Saturday nights as some angered customers have called for a boycott, according to The Boston Globe.
The backlash came as the bar was already struggling financially under to the bar’s unusual business model that includes rules such as "Nobody will be barred from entry due to lack of funds."

Last Ditch also had the mask mandate in place as part of a policy intended to make the space accessible to disabled and immunocompromised patrons, meaning the face covering requirement was designed to protect anyone who was immunocompromised.
Customers were told that they were expected to mask up unless they were actively taking a bite of food or a sip of a drink.
The bar’s owners began to fall behind on their bills and were unable to pay themselves or even their staff.
Jackie Matellian, the remaining owner involved in daily operations, lived in her truck for six months, working four jobs and carrying a $50,000 loan, according to The Boston Globe.
ONLINE FURY ERUPTS AS CONSERVATIVES RECALL ’INSANE’ COVID-19 LOCKDOWN POLICIES AFTER FAUCI TAKES THE FIFTH
Last Ditch Bar and Arts Venue recently removed its mask requirements on Saturdays in an effort to boost business. (Google Maps)
The two other owners stepped back from daily operations months ago, including one who had enrolled in clown school and another who is a drag performer using it/its pronouns.
Because of the financial woes, the bar decided to lift the mask mandate on Saturdays to increase revenue and keep the business afloat, The Boston Globe reported.
"It is with love we inform our immunocompromised disabled divas we will be opening Saturday nights as mask optional," Last Ditch wrote on an August Instagram post that ignited the backlash.

The bar first attempted to ease tensions and apologize for its post, writing: "We are sorry for our passive and dismissive tone of our change to the norms and schedule impacting the most intersectional of us. We understand everyone faces different intersections and we are always working to consider all needs fully."

But that did little to lower the temperature, as critics said Last Ditch’s post failed to include written "alt text," a short written description of an image added to the HTML code of a webpage for visually impaired people.
"This is not an accessible post," one person commented. "It indicates the lack of care or interest in Disability intersectionality."
Last Ditch again sought to address the controversy during its monthly community meeting on Sept. 11, according to The Boston Globe.
Outraged attendees who were joined by Zoom began flooding the chat with comments that were read aloud for the in-person group to hear.
The meeting took another twist when critics made an allegation of racism because the mediator, a licensed therapist, was white.

"A lot of people are calling for an acknowledgment of harm and I’m hearing a WHITE therapist … center[ing] the feelings of a majority white and white adjacent staff," one person said, the newspaper reported.

Attendees also took issue with a therapist being there at all and said it made them feel "widely unsafe" since that made the woman a mandated reporter, meaning she is required by law to report known or suspected abuse.

Matellian broke down in tears when it was her turn to speak, saying she was only trying to help her friends with the bar before taking over once they left and having a difficult time trying to survive financially.
Matellian has fallen behind on rent and the bar’s landlord wants $3,900 by the end of September.
"It was not my passion project," Matellian cried while masked up. "I never really wanted this. I don’t think I’m doing a very good job."
MASSACHUSETTS LAWMAKERS PASS BILL TO SCRAP 'OFFENSIVE LANGUAGE' FROM STATE'S GENERAL LAWS
Some critics accused the bar's owners of putting disabled people at risk. (Google Maps)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
But the bar's critics had no sympathy for the struggling business owner.
"You chose to use your time to spill tears and center your feelings," one person responded. "This is incredibly racist and deflecting behavior."
The mask-optional Saturday nights have not helped with business, as the barroom has been nearly empty each weekend despite drink deals and DJs that would attract dozens of customers in the past.
One person recently suggested having a Lady Gaga-themed party to pull in more patrons.
"Gaga is canceled," the bartender said. "Gaga is Zionist."

title: Texas man charged with capital murder after 5-year-old killed in roadway shooting
summary: Jeremy Porter was charged with capital murder after police said he killed 5-year-old Zah'Layah Walter in a roadway shooting in northwest Harris County.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A Texas man has been arrested and charged with capital murder in connection with a roadway shooting that killed a 5-year-old girl over the weekend, authorities said.

Jeremy Porter, 47, was taken into custody and booked into the Harris County Jail in Houston after investigators identified him as the suspect in the fatal shooting of Zah'Layah Walter, according to Harris County Sheriff Ed Gonzalez.
Investigators used evidence, including information obtained through automated license plate readers, to identify Porter, who was arrested less than 24 hours after the shooting, authorities said.
MISSOURI MOM WHO PUT NEWBORN IN OVEN INSTEAD OF CRIB LEARNS FATE AS MURDER CHARGE DROPPED
Zah'Layah Walter, 5, was killed in a roadway shooting in northwest Harris County, Texas, on Sept. 19, 2026. (Harris County Sheriff Ed Gonzalez via Facebook)

The shooting happened Saturday night in northwest Harris County, where Zah'Layah was riding in a vehicle with her mother, Monica Hicks, and her four siblings when someone opened fire on the family's vehicle, the sheriff's office said.
Authorities said bullets struck the vehicle, killing the 5-year-old.
SISTER OF MISSING DC MOM SPEAKS OUT AFTER EX’S ARREST EXPOSES 'HORRIFYING' ABUSIVE RELATIONSHIP
Jeremy Porter, 47, was taken into custody and booked into the Harris County Jail. (Harris County Sheriff's Office via Facebook)
Hicks told local outlet KHOU she was driving home from her mother's house with her five children when someone began shooting at the family's vehicle on Grant Road near Jones Road.
"All my kids in the back seat were screaming, and they continued to shoot in my car. And I did not know my daughter was hit until I pulled into my apartment," Hicks said.
The Harris County Sheriff's Office said the investigation remains ongoing.
MARYLAND HUNTER'S ALLEGED MISTAKE LEAVES DELAWARE MOTHER DEAD
The Harris County Sheriff's Office said it remains "committed to seeking justice for [Zah'Layah] and supporting her family." (Harris County Sheriff's Office via X)

"We stood alongside the family of 5-year-old Zay’Layah Walter, whose life was tragically taken in a roadway-related shooting. The person accused of taking her life has been arrested," the Harris County Sheriff's Office wrote on X on Tuesday. "We remain committed to seeking justice for [Zah'Layah] and supporting her family."

title: Missouri mom who put newborn in oven instead of crib learns fate as murder charge dropped
summary: Mariah Thomas told Kansas City police she mistook the oven for a crib. The infant was found with severe burns across her body in February 2024.
story: Fox News senior correspondent Mike Tobin reports on the investigation into the death of a 2-year-old Illinois boy and the detention of his mother, Corie Walsh.

A Missouri mother who said she accidentally put her 1-month-old baby in an oven instead of a crib will spend more than a decade behind bars after reaching a deal that wiped away a first-degree murder charge.

Mariah Thomas, 28, pleaded guilty Tuesday to first-degree endangering the welfare of a child resulting in death and was ordered to serve 13 years in the Missouri Department of Corrections, according to Jackson County court records.
The punishment came more than two years after Kansas City police found Thomas' infant daughter dead with severe burns inside a city home.
NEW MEXICO WOMAN'S BODYCAM CONFESSION ABOUT HIDING NEWBORN BABY IN HOSPITAL GARBAGE TOSSED BY STATE COURT

Mariah Thomas received a 13-year prison sentence after pleading guilty to endangering the welfare of a child resulting in death. A first-degree murder charge was dismissed under her plea agreement. (Jackson County Detention Center)

Thomas was also charged with first-degree murder, but that count was dismissed as part of the plea agreement, court records show. She received no probation and will be credited for time already served.
The nightmare unfolded on Feb. 9, 2024, after officers were called to the home around 1:30 p.m. on charges involving a report of a baby who was not breathing, according to charging documents.
Police arrived to find the 1-month-old child with apparent burns across her body. Kansas City Fire Department personnel pronounced her dead at the scene.
Investigators were told Thomas had gone to put her daughter down for a nap but "accidentally placed her in the oven instead of the crib," the documents state.
FLORIDA 3-YEAR-OLD DIES AFTER TRAGIC INCIDENT INVOLVING COMMON PLAY TOY AT BABYSITTER'S HOUSE
The punishment came more than two years after Kansas City police found Thomas' infant daughter dead with severe burns inside a city home. (Kansas City Missouri Police Department, File)
A family member later told detectives that Thomas said, "I thought I put [her] in her crib and I accidentally put her in the oven."

The child was wearing a bodysuit over a diaper, and investigators said her clothing appeared to have melted onto the diaper. Police also recovered a baby blanket with significant burn marks from the living room, according to the probable cause statement.
The infant was identified by FOX 4 Kansas City as Za'riah Thomas.

Thomas initially declined to speak with detectives after being advised of her rights, but she agreed to provide a blood sample and allow investigators to access data from her cellphone, the documents state.
STARVING TODDLER ATE DIAPERS AND DRYWALL BEFORE DYING IN FILTHY ROOM WHILE PARENTS LIVED CLEAN, POLICE SAY
A baby monitor camera sits above a crib in a nursery in a California home. (Tech Trends/Gado/Getty Images)
Then-Jackson County Prosecutor Jean Peters Baker called the child's death a "gruesome" tragedy when the original charge was announced in February 2024.

"We acknowledge the gruesome nature of this tragedy, and our hearts are weighted by the loss of this precious life," Baker said at the time. "We trust the criminal justice system to respond appropriately to these awful circumstances."
The original complaint charged Thomas only with first-degree endangering the welfare of a child resulting in death.
Court records show prosecutors later added the first-degree murder count that was ultimately dismissed under Tuesday's agreement.
NORTH DAKOTA MOM STABS HER 2 CHILDREN TO DEATH IN 'HORRIFIC' KILLING THAT LEFT COPS TRAUMATIZED: OFFICIALS
Judge Sarah A. Castle found Thomas entered the guilty plea freely and voluntarily and understood the charge and consequences. The judgment states Thomas had no mental disease or defect defense.

Thomas was returned to the Jackson County sheriff’s custody to await transfer to state prison. The judge also ordered her to pay $68 to Missouri’s Crime Victims’ Compensation Fund and waived all other court costs.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Jackson County prosecutor's office for comment.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Bodycam footage captures moments after ICE shooting of Venezuelan migrant in Austin
summary: Austin Police Department body camera footage captures the moments after an ICE officer shot a Venezuelan migrant during an arrest attempt.
story: Bodycam footage released by the Austin Police Department shows the aftermath of the shooting of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez (Credit: Austin Police Department).

The Austin Police Department on Tuesday released body camera footage showing the arrest of an illegal Venezuelan immigrant who was shot moments earlier by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers over the weekend.
Three short videos detail the local police response to the shooting of 28-year-old Wilber Rafael Garces Perez on Sunday as ICE officers attempted to take him into custody.

In one video, what sounds like three gunshots can be heard. Another clip shows an officer arriving at the scene, where Garces Perez is seen sitting hunched over in the driver's seat of his vehicle and appearing to grab his left shoulder in pain.
DEM REACTIONS WITHIN MOMENTS OF AUSTIN ICE SHOOTING SPARK VIRAL OUTRAGE LOCALLY, ONLINE: 'DISQUALIFYING'

Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, 28, was shot as U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers were trying to take him into custody in Austin, Texas over the weekend. Austin police bodycam footage released Tuesday shows Garces Perez in his vehicle after the shooting, just before he was arrested. (Austin Police Department)
Officers wearing body cameras assisted Garces Perez out of the vehicle, contradicting claims that he was pulled out by agents, before placing him under arrest.
Another officer is heard ordering someone to get a pair of shears to cut open Garces Perez's shirt to examine his wounds.
ICE RESUMES NATIONWIDE TRAFFIC STOPS UNDER NEW POLICY REQUIRING BODY CAMERAS
Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, 28, an illegal immigrant from Venezuela, was shot by U.S. Immigration (ICE) and Customs Enforcement officers in Austin, Texas over the weekend. (Wilber Garces / Facebook)
"¿Tiene armas?" an officer asks in Spanish, inquiring if Garces Perez has any firearms.
"No," Garces Perez replies.
"He's got… looks like one gunshot wound so far," an officer is heard saying.

Garces Perez was reportedly delivering a DoorDash order when he made a U-turn under a highway before ICE agents continued to pursue him. His attorney, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, claimed an unmarked truck chased her client and sideswiped his vehicle before he was shot.

Authorities confirmed Garces Perez had a final order of removal. However, Lincoln-Goldfinch said her client received the order after a hearing notice was sent to his previous address, despite him having updated his address with the court.
ICE has disputed rumors surrounding the shooting and Garces Perez's legal status, noting that his work permit expired in 2025 and that holding one does not confer legal status in the United States.

The agency also stated that Garces Perez was released from the hospital and arrived at an ICE detention facility just hours later, where he slept on a bed. ICE rebuffed allegations that Garces Perez was indiscriminately targeted.

title: Former news anchor working for California Democrat arrested by immigration authorities at Las Vegas airport
summary: Ho-Yin Mo, a legislative aide to California Assemblywoman Catherine Stefani, was arrested by federal immigration authorities at Las Vegas airport over an alleged visa overstay.
story: California lawmakers consider a bill banning former Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents from holding public security positions. Trump Media senior comms advisor Katie Zacharia joins host Trace Gallagher to discuss the legislative push targeting federal law enforcement officers.
A staffer for a California Democratic state lawmaker was arrested by federal immigration authorities in Las Vegas, according to reports.

Ho-Yin Mo, who was a news anchor at a Chinese-language news station in San Francisco before becoming a legislative aide to California Assemblywoman Catherine Stefani, was taken into custody Thursday at Harry Reid International Airport.

"On January 13, 2020, Mo lawfully entered the U.S. on a temporary basis but illegally overstayed his welcome by failing to depart by May 15, 2020," the Department of Homeland Security told Fox News Digital. "Work authorization or a pending application do NOT confer legal status in the United States."

Mo joined Stefani's office in January 2025, according to his LinkedIn profile.
"No one is above the law, not even the California legislature and its staff," First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California Bill Essayli wrote on X.

title: Bryan Kohberger didn't understand what he was doing when he pleaded guilty: unsealed memo
summary: Bryan Kohberger's former attorneys said he struggled to rationally understand court proceedings before his guilty plea in the Idaho murders case.
story: Idaho prosecutors urge a judge to reject murder suspect Bryan Kohberger's attempt to withdraw his guilty plea, calling the defense's arguments a fishing expedition. Former federal prosecutor Jonathan Fahey joins to break down the latest legal maneuvers, the strength of the state's case and what lies ahead for the victims' families in the high-profile trial.

FIRST ON FOX: Bryan Kohberger's former attorneys told an Idaho judge before his plea deal that their client struggled to "rationally understand" what was unfolding in court and to make "consequential decisions" concerning his case, including whether to testify in his own defense or to accept a plea deal, according to newly unsealed court filings.

"The memo is pretty clear that there's a serious issue there that shows different reasons why that plea might not have been accepted," Kohberger's new attorney, Greg Rauch, told Fox News Digital. "Those issues have to be flushed out and explored.
Although the memo's Tuesday release appeared to have surprised him, he said he initially filed it under seal out of an abundance of caution and to avoid running afoul of previous orders in the case.

Kohberger, a 31-year-old former criminology Ph.D. student, is serving four consecutive sentences of life in prison without the possibility of parole, plus another 10 years. Rauch was assigned to his case over the summer and did not represent him as it initially played out.
BRYAN KOHBERGER'S BID TO OUST JUDGE AND UNDO GUILTY PLEA MOVES FORWARD WITH NEW COURT DATE SET

Bryan Kohberger at the Ada County Courthouse after his sentencing hearing, July 23, 2025, in Boise, Idaho, for brutally stabbing four University of Idaho students to death nearly three years earlier. (AP Photo/Kyle Green, Pool)

"In the May 20 [2025] ex parte supplement, counsel advised the Court that Kohberger was having difficulty comprehending adverse rulings and discerning their effect upon the case as a whole," the newly published memo reads. "Counsel represented that, despite the accumulation of significant rulings concerning the death penalty, suppression issues, and motions in limine, Kohberger was having difficulty meaningfully incorporating those developments into a rational assessment of the case and its potential outcomes."

In the memo, which was filed under seal in support of a prior motion to disqualify the judge, Rauch described his goal as not to show that Kohberger was incompetent but to bolster his argument that the judge may be biased.

"Before June 26, [2025,] the Court knew that counsel was asking for additional time not only to review evidence and continue investigation, but also to investigate Kohberger’s ability to rationally understand and make consequential decisions and to obtain expert assistance in communicating with him about whether to resolve the case short of trial," Rauch wrote to the court in a document that remained sealed for nearly a month.

Kohberger's original defense team sought more time for an inquiry into his ability to understand the proceedings but "expressly denied" that he was incompetent.
Judge Steven Hippler on Tuesday ordered the Aug. 27 memo to be unsealed after rejecting Kohberger's reasoning for keeping the document withheld from the public.

"The Court disagrees that the information contained in the Supplemental Memorandum is intimate, protected or will result in harm if disclosed," Hippler wrote. "It simply describes in very general terms trial counsel's concerns about Petitioner's difficulty in comprehending adverse rulings and understanding their effect on the outcome of the case."

Judge Steven Hippler speaks at the sentencing hearing of Bryan Kohberger at the Ada County Courthouse July 23, 2025, in Boise, Idaho. (Kyle Green/AP Photo, Pool)

Kohberger's former defense team, led by Anne Taylor, had sought more time for discovery as his trial approached last year. According to the unsealed filing, they were also quietly seeking help for Kohberger to understand the proceedings.

summary: Antoinette Forbes’ former partner was arrested last week, but authorities have not confirmed whether his case is connected to her disappearance.
story: Antoinette Forbes’ sister said she learned about the "horrifying" 2021 assault after Russell Ashford, Antoinette’s ex, was arrested last week.

The sister of missing D.C. mother Antoinette Forbes revealed that she was unaware Antoinette had been in an abusive relationship until details of a 2021 assault surfaced following the arrest of the father of her 10-year-old son.

Russell Ashford, 65, who was detained last week in Pennsylvania, reportedly took unauthorized overnight custody of their son on the night Antoinette was last seen, according to the Montgomery County District Attorney's Office. He also allegedly violated his probation stemming from the 2021 assault case, the office said. Authorities did not name Ashford as a suspect in Antoinette's disappearance.

"Antoinette did not tell us at all about the assault in 2021, so just wrapping our minds around that, it's unfathomable. We can't really conceive it," Antoinette’s sister, Aileen, said in an interview with Fox News Digital.
"I didn't hear about them until I saw some excerpts of the report after my sister went missing."
FAMILY OF CRITICALLY MISSING DC MOTHER SAYS POLICE STILL TREATING HOME AS ACTIVE CRIME SCENE
Antoinette Forbes smiles during a photo with her sister, Aileen. (Courtesy of the Family and Friends of Antoinette Forbes)
According to Maryland court filings, Ashford pleaded guilty to first-degree assault in 2021.

During an argument over their child's schooling, Ashford allegedly threw Antoinette against the staircase, repeatedly punched her while she was lying on the kitchen floor and banged her head against the ground at least a dozen times until she lost consciousness, according to court filings.
The assault continued until a neighbor heard her screaming and entered the home to intervene.

After Antoinette was taken to a hospital, tests showed she suffered multiple facial lacerations, multiple fractured facial bones, eye damage, a concussion, a broken finger and bruising, court documents said. Prosecutors said the assault left Antoinette with permanent eye and hand injuries.
After pleading guilty, Ashford was sentenced to 15 years in prison but served only nine months and five years' probation upon release, authorities said.
Aileen said the reports came as a shock to her and her family, who are still processing the revelation.

"The report is horrifying. And to tell the truth, I haven't had the time to fully process that. Just the thought of my sister enduring such a brutal attack is just deeply hurtful to me and to the rest of my family. We don't want to, we can't even conceive of it," Aileen said.
FEDS PLAN NEW BAHAMAS SEARCH FOR LYNETTE HOOKER AFTER GPS DATA ALLEGEDLY TORPEDOES HUSBAND’S STORY: SOURCE
Antoinette Forbes sits alongside her son. (Courtesy of the Family and Friends of Antoinette Forbes)
Aileen noted that Antoinette may have kept the abuse from her family because she was protective of the people she loved.
"Antoinette, she wanted to protect us from it. She did not want us to have any involvement with Russell," Aileen said.
More than two weeks have passed since Antoinette was last seen on Friday, Sept. 4, just one week before she planned to take her son to visit their relatives in California, Aileen said.
Antoinette was reported missing on Sept. 6 after friends found her dog, car, phone and wallet inside the home, but no sign of her.
Antoinette Forbes poses for a picture while standing in an empty cobblestone street. (Courtesy of the Family and Friends of Antoinette Forbes)

Shortly after her disappearance, Ashford was arrested for allegedly violating his probation, which strictly prohibited him from having hostile contact with Antoinette or their child, amid the concerning circumstances surrounding Antoinette's disappearance, court documents said.

On July 16, 2026, Ashford reportedly arrived unannounced at his son's summer camp, but staff informed him he was not on the approved pickup list and asked for identification. Ashford allegedly became agitated and forceful with a counselor, prompting staff to file a formal written report about the incident.
Pennsylvania State Police told Fox News Digital that Ashford was arrested after a traffic stop revealed he had an active warrant tied to the July incident.
Authorities told Fox News Digital last week that the search for Antoinette is ongoing and that officials do not have any updates to share with the public.

Aileen further urged anyone living in the Nebraska Avenue Northwest neighborhood where Antoinette lived to check their security cameras and think back to anything that may have seemed peculiar.

"Just check it, try to jog your memory," Aileen pleaded. "Was there something that seemed peculiar that might be something that you can come forward with and offer a detail to the authorities? It might make a difference."

"To everyone who has been following this devastating story and who has been a part of the search for Antoinette, who showed up at the vigil, who's contributed to our GoFundMe account… I just want to say a deep thank you because it's so meaningful to me and our family."
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Impeached Georgia mayor speaks out after sexting, spending scandals result in ouster
summary: Ex-Stockbridge, Georgia Mayor Jayden Williams, 23, who was ousted earlier this month, told WSB-TV that he did not expect to be booted out of office.
story: Jayden Williams faced intense questioning during an investigative hearing over his relationship and communications with an 18-year-old high school student involved in a city-affiliated mentorship program. (City of Stockbridge Government)
Former Stockbridge, Georgia Mayor Jayden Williams did not expect to be ousted from office earlier this month amid scrutiny over alleged misconduct.
"I didn't expect this," he told WSB-TV. "You know, maybe a censure, but definitely not a removal."

Williams, 23, who had served in the role for less than a year at the time he was given the boot, was the city's youngest mayor ever. His tenure was cut short amid allegations pertaining to his spending of city funds as well as a relationship with an 18-year-old high school student.
GEORGIA MAYOR, 23, OUSTED 10 MONTHS AFTER MAKING HISTORY AS STATE'S YOUNGEST MAYOR

Jayden Williams, then-Mayor of Stockbridge, speaks onstage during Juneteenth At The Bridge With Common at VyStar Amphitheater at The Bridge on June 19, 2026, in Stockbridge, Ga. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images)
Pressed by WSB-TV whether he should have recognized that the relationship was inappropriate, Williams said, "I would have to somewhat agree to that."
"There was no violation of the oath," Williams told the outlet. "I wasn't even mayor yet."
WSB-TV reported that Williams said the relationship was not sexual.

Jayden L. Williams, then-Mayor of Stockbridge GA, speaks onstage during the 2nd Annual Ologo Golf Tournament hosted by Ne-Yo at Eagles Landing Country Club on April 6, 2026, in Stockbridge, Ga. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images)
NBC News previously reported that Williams admitted he had exchanged nude photos.
"That’s not abnormal for somebody my age," Williams said during a city council meeting, according to the outlet.
A police report noted that Williams did not commit any criminal violations because the student was considered an adult under Georgia law.
Williams acknowledged spending some funds on personal purchases. He said they were from the mayor's reallocated $5,000 annual budget, not the city's general fund, according to WSB-TV.
"It was not intentional and I paid it back immediately," he said.
Jayden Williams, then-Mayor of Stockbridge attends "Da 'Partments 2" Atlanta Screening at Atlantic Station on July 9, 2026, in Atlanta, Ga. (Prince Williams/WireImage)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
He noted that the city purchasing card was similar in appearance to his personal card, according to Fox 5. He later replaced the cards to avoid future confusion, the outlet reported.

Williams became the youngest Black mayor elected in Georgia history after campaigning for the position while still attending Clark Atlanta University. He was impeached by the Stockbridge City Council earlier this month after taking office in January.
Alex Nitzberg is a writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Nolan Wells' friends cleared by grand jury as their lawyers vow to hold online accusers accountable
summary: A Mississippi grand jury found Nolan Wells' death consistent with drowning and no evidence of a crime or racial motive in the Horn Island case.
story: Jackson County District Attorney Angel Myers McIlrath said a grand jury found "absolutely no evidence" that Nolan Wells' death was racially motivated, calling the viral narrative around the 19-year-old's Horn Island drowning "false."

After a Mississippi grand jury found that Nolan Wells' death was "consistent with drowning" and turned up no evidence of a crime or racial motive, an attorney for one of the men wrongly targeted online said his client intends to hold the accusers accountable.

Wells, 19, disappeared July 4 after taking a boat trip to Horn Island, a barrier island along Mississippi's Gulf Coast, with a group of friends. Search crews combed the area for two days until a National Park Service ranger discovered his remains at the island's northwestern tip on July 6.
Months later, a Jackson County, Mississippi, grand jury returned a "no true bill" in Wells' death investigation, meaning no indictment or charges will be filed.
"The Grand Jury finds that the position of, the condition of, time of discovery, and location of Mr. Wells' remains is consistent with drowning," the grand jury wrote.
In a statement to Fox News Digital, Russell Latino, who represents Bart Edmiston and his family, said: "This story involves two tragedies.
SEARCH CALLED OFF AFTER BODY MATCHING MISSING TEEN NOLAN WELLS FOUND OFF MISSISSIPPI COAST
Nolan Wells smiles on the field while playing wide receiver for Southwest Mississippi Community College. (Christine Wonsley/Facebook)

"The death of Nolan Wells is a tragedy. So too is the way his friends, his community and his state were maligned by unscrupulous charlatans and grifters who spread false and malicious lies," Latino said. "The grand jury, made up of Mississippians of all races and backgrounds, did its solemn duty. But to anyone who knew the actual facts, not reckless garbage spewed on the internet, the result of the process was never in doubt. The Edmiston family looks forward to bringing accountability to those who exploited tragedy to divide and injure. They continue to pray for healing, for the family of Nolan and for their precious community."

Edmiston and other friends of Wells' were subjected to months of online rumors and speculation that they were somehow criminally responsible for the then-18-year-old's death. The grand jury and Jackson County District Attorney Angel Myers McIlrath both concluded those allegations were baseless.
Edward Andrew Paltzik, who represents three of Wells' friends, had a pointed message for attorney Ben Crump.
"@AttorneyCrump NO TRUE BILL. You should apologize immediately to completely innocent young men Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo, and Morgan Seymour. You have some serious explaining to do!" Paltzik said.
He said he's also sent several legal notices to social media influencers and media figures on behalf of three men he represents.
In a video statement Monday, Jackson County District Attorney Angel Myers McIlrath said there was "absolutely no evidence" that Wells' death was due to his race.
Fox News Digital has reached out to Crump for comment.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

"The narrative that three White boys and a Black boy went to an island and only three White friends returned spread like wildfire. This was false," McIlrath said. "There is absolutely no evidence to support the allegations that Nolan's disappearance and death were racially motivated."
"Nolan's friends loved Nolan and Nolan loved them. Nolan chose to stay on the island that day, and there is not a scintilla of evidence to contradict that," she said.
NOLAN WELLS' HOMETOWN OFFICIALS RALLY BEHIND SHERIFF AFTER 'DERELICT IN THEIR DUTIES' ATTACK
READ THE GRAND JURY REPORT:
McIlrath also sharply criticized attorney Ben Crump's team, which she said knew early on that the death wasn't racially motivated.

"The family, the Crump team, and anyone close to Nolan knew that his disappearance and death were not the result of racial hate or violence," she said. "What I am suggesting is that the Crump team knew better but did not do better."
SEND US A TIP
Nolan Xavier Wells disappeared on the Fourth of July while boating with friends, according to authorities. (Jackson County Sheriff's Department via Facebook)
According to the district attorney, the family's legal team advised her office in August that it had uncovered no evidence a crime was committed against Wells.

"On August 13th, 2026, after the Crump team conducted and released the results of its independent autopsy and after receiving hundreds of tips, they advised my office that they had no evidence of a crime being committed against Nolan Wells," she said.
CAJUN NAVY LEADER WARNS NOLAN WELLS' SEARCH AREA HAS DEADLY 'WASHING MACHINE' CURRENTS: 'LOTS OF DROWNINGS'

Lawyers representing Wells' family disputed the decision in a statement to Fox News Digital. Civil rights attorney Ben Crump said the state was closing the case before the truth had been established, citing bruising on the back of Wells' head and an independent autopsy that he said documented blunt force injuries to Wells' head and back. Crump said neither the family nor the state has determined how Wells died, and he urged the Justice Department to open an investigation if Mississippi declines to do so.

"Today, the State of Mississippi is attempting to close the chapter on Nolan Wells’ death without getting to the truth," Crump said. "We are releasing the final independent autopsy report in its entirety, so everyone can read it for themselves. This grand jury result leaves us with more questions than answers. Nolan’s family will not rest until we know what happened to him, and neither will we."
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Both the Mississippi Chief Medical Examiner and the family's pathologist, Dr. Roger Mitchell, who performed a second autopsy for the Wells family agreed that while the cause of death is undetermined, "drowning is a diagnosis of exclusion." That means the conclusion was reached by ruling out other causes rather than by direct evidence of drowning.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

The grand jury didn't find any evidence suggesting a crime occurred, or that Wells' death was motivated by race, and also took direct aim at the theories circulating on social media about the people on the boats.
GOVERNOR BLAMES ACTIVISTS IN NOLAN WELLS CASE FOR ‘STOKING DIVISION,’ OFFICIAL SAYS FBI PROBING THREATS

Attorney Ben Crump, center, speaks next to Elmore and Christine Wonsley, at left, and Rev. Al Sharpton during a memorial service for Nolan Xavier Wells, an 18-year-old found dead after taking a July 4 boat trip with friends, Monday, July 20, 2026, in Ocean Springs, Miss. (AP Photo/Gerald Herbert)

"The Grand Jury finds no credible evidence to support the public allegations that any persons who rode to or from Horn Island on July 4, 2026, on the Triton, the Palm Beach, or the Tideline engaged in any criminal conduct related to the death of Mr. Wells," the grand jury wrote. "The allegations against the occupants of the Triton, the Palm Beach, and the Tideline are not based in truth, and are solely the result of public clamor and private malice."
NOLAN WELLS INDEPENDENT AUTOPSY DOESN'T POINT TO FOUL PLAY, FORMER MEDICAL EXAMINER SAYS

Among the many questions surrounding Wells' death was an apparent injury to the back of his head, where bruising was found. A witness testified that he saw Wells slip off a boat, but the grand jury said it could not confirm the fall caused the bruising.
CALIFORNIA MAN ARRESTED FOR ALLEGEDLY SENDING BOMB THREAT TO JUDGE IN NOLAN WELLS' DEATH CASE: DOCS
Jackson County District Attorney Angel Myers McIlrath delivers a video statement on the grand jury's findings in the death investigation of Nolan Wells. (Jackson County District Attorney)

"A witness testified under oath that he saw Mr. Wells slip awkwardly off the side of a boat around the time of 3:30 p.m. on July 4, 2026, but could not say whether Mr. Wells struck his head during the fall. The witness testified that Mr. Wells continued to socialize after the fall and did not appear injured," the grand jury report said.

The 23 grand jurors who heard the case included 12 White people, five African Americans, two Hispanics, two Native Americans, one Asian and one who identified as "other."
Adam Sabes is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to Adam.Sabes@fox.com and on Twitter @asabes10.

title: Dad of 'American Idol' contestant's slain wife made eerie Google search after hearing of her murder
summary: Caleb Flynn's murder trial revealed how Ohio investigators searched storm drains, attics and vehicles for the gun allegedly used to kill Ashley Flynn.
story: Witness Kayla Keyt recalls the night Ashley was shot in Tipp City, Ohio. She details the defendant Caleb's explanation of the events, raising questions about his story and why Ashley was targeted.

Investigators hunting for the gun prosecutors say former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn used to kill his wife brought in an ATF firearms-detection dog to scour woods, fields and the family home – but the alleged murder weapon still hasn't been found.

ATF Special Agent David McMullen testified Tuesday that his K-9 partner, Hilton, spent hours searching around Flynn's Tipp City, Ohio, home, through nearby woods and along a walking path before combing a farm field for the missing firearm.
The dog was later brought inside the garage and home to search areas where a weapon could have been hidden, McMullen testified.
‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT’S 100K TEXTS WITH MISTRESS SHOW MOTIVE IN WIFE’S MURDER, PROSECUTORS SAY
The first search lasted roughly three hours before Hilton became exhausted. McMullen and the dog returned the following day and searched the property, woods and farm field again.

Caleb Flynn becomes emotional in court during his murder trial in Ohio. Flynn is accused of killing his wife, Ashley Flynn, in February 2026 and staging the scene to look like a break-in. (COURTESY: WKEF)
Both searches came up empty.

Flynn is accused of fatally shooting his wife, Ashley Flynn, inside the couple's home on Feb. 16 before staging the scene to look like an intruder had broken in. He has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and other charges.

The ATF search adds another layer to the lengths investigators went to try to find the missing gun, after jurors heard Monday about searches involving storm drains, a high-powered magnet, vehicles and attic insulation.

The expanded search was one of several developments Tuesday, as jurors also heard about the couple's finances, a life insurance policy on Ashley and two devices belonging to Flynn's alleged mistress that investigators never recovered.
‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT’S 100K TEXTS WITH MISTRESS SHOW MOTIVE IN WIFE’S MURDER, PROSECUTORS SAY

The trial also turned deeply personal Tuesday as Ashley's mother and sister took the stand, describing the family's frantic first hours after her death and the stunning revelation that Flynn had allegedly been having an affair with a woman they knew from church.
Ashley Flynn’s mother, Jill Smith, testifies during Caleb Flynn’s murder trial in Ohio on Sept. 22, 2026. (Credit: WKEF)

Ashley's mother, Jill Smith, testified that her phone rang around 3 a.m. the morning her daughter was killed. She initially thought it was her husband, who was traveling, but saw Flynn's name on the screen instead.
"She's gone," Smith recalled Flynn telling her.
When Smith asked who he meant, Flynn responded, "Ashley, she's gone," before telling her, "Someone broke in and shot her," she testified.
WATCH: Ashley Flynn's mother Jill Smith testifies about defendant Caleb telling daughters mom was hurt
Smith said she told Flynn she was coming to the house, but he told her police were there and she could not come. She hung up, became dizzy and lay down on the bathroom floor.
"It seemed like forever," Smith testified, saying she remained there for about five minutes before getting up and calling her husband to tell him Ashley had been killed.
‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT’S 100K TEXTS WITH MISTRESS SHOW MOTIVE IN WIFE’S MURDER, PROSECUTORS SAY
Smith drove to the home anyway and said seeing the flashing police lights made the reality of what had happened sink in.
Ashley Flynn’s sister, Kayla Keyt, testifies during Caleb Flynn’s murder trial in Ohio on Sept. 22, 2026. (Credit: WKEF)
"And then I knew it was true," she testified.

Flynn later came outside shaking, Smith said. The two hugged before sitting on the front porch, where she became concerned enough about him that she asked for a blanket and suggested someone call an EMT because she feared he was going into shock.
While Smith was comforting Flynn, her husband, Todd Smith, testified that he was already questioning Flynn’s account as he made the roughly 16-hour drive home from Canada.

Todd said the alleged break-in story "just didn't make sense" to him, prompting him to Google whether a "Christian man" could "snap and shoot his wife." He testified that he called Jill and told her, "This really doesn’t look good on Caleb," but she responded, "Don’t even go there."
WATCH: Kayla Keyt testifies on family business and defendant Caleb Flynn
Ashley's sister, Kayla Keyt, testified that she initially believed so strongly in Flynn's innocence that she told investigators "100%" they had arrested the wrong man.
"I trusted Caleb with everything I had in me," Keyt testified.
Keyt said she became angry when she initially heard rumors that Flynn had been having an affair because she believed they were unfairly damaging his reputation.
"I was so mad because it was tarnishing his reputation," Keyt said. "I just knew in my heart that he was completely innocent. I really believed that with all of my heart."
FBI JOINS PROBE IN MURDER OF CHRISTIAN TEACHER SHOT IN OHIO HOME AS 'AMERICAN IDOL' HUSBAND, CHILDREN SLEPT
Keyt testified that changed when investigators told her Flynn had been having an affair with Alleigha, a woman the family knew from Christian Life Center.

Ashley Flynn, a Tipp City Schools substitute teacher and volleyball coach, was found dead in her Ohio home during reported burglary. Police launch homicide investigation into her death. (Tipp City Schools)

Alleigha was the church's main worship leader and performed alongside Flynn, who sang with the worship team during rehearsals and weekend services, Keyt testified. She said she personally knew Alleigha casually from seeing her at church.
"I don't think I've been more shocked in my life," Keyt said.

Keyt recalled asking investigators, "Are you 100% sure?" and said she had them repeat it two or three times because she "could not even fathom" Flynn having an affair. She testified that she first learned about it during an FBI interview the morning after Flynn's arrest.
Keyt, who testified that Ashley's two daughters now live with her family, said the girls have since learned about the alleged affair and personally knew Alleigha.
"They were mostly brokenhearted for mommy," Keyt testified.
Keyt said the girls were shocked and questioned why their father did not love their mother as much as Ashley loved him.
Caleb Flynn, 49, was arraigned in court on Friday, Feb. 20. (Dayton Daily News)
But when the girls were told who Flynn had allegedly been involved with, Keyt recalled the older daughter's response: "I'm not surprised."
The defense later focused on two devices belonging to Alleigha that police were unable to recover.

Tipp City Police Capt. Tony Smith testified that investigators learned Alleigha's work laptop went missing during a Florida trip in January 2026, about a month before Ashley was killed, while her cellphone was dropped in water during the same trip.
WATCH: Ashley Flynn's mother Jill Smith testifies about learning of her daughter's murder from Caleb
Neither device was recovered.
Investigators obtained the laptop's make, model and serial number and passed the information to an investigative team that included Tipp City detectives, the FBI and Ohio BCI, Smith testified.
Jurors also heard testimony Tuesday about the Flynns' finances and a life insurance policy on Ashley.
EX-AMERICAN IDOL CONTESTANT CHARGED IN WIFE'S MURDER PREVIOUSLY DESCRIBED AS ‘VERY TALENTED’ CHURCH LEADER
Smith testified investigators identified a $100,000 life insurance policy on Ashley that was owned by Flynn, who was also the sole beneficiary.
Bank records introduced by prosecutors showed Flynn and Ashley had $84,369.29 in a joint savings account on the day she was killed.
A Tipp City mother of two was found dead after a reported home invasion. (Ashley Flynn/Facebook)
Ashley's father, Todd Smith, testified that Flynn earned $195,000 in 2025 working in sales for the family's commercial flooring business, along with roughly $10,000 in medical reimbursements.
Smith said he planned to eventually give the business to Ashley and Keyt, with each daughter owning half. He testified that Flynn's income had the potential to increase if sales continued to grow.
The new testimony came after jurors spent much of Monday hearing about the exhaustive search for the missing gun and forensic evidence collected from the Flynn home.
Detective Adam Bernard walked jurors through the lengths investigators went to as they searched for the missing firearm in the days after Ashley's death.
Police searched the backyard and nearby wooded areas before turning their attention underground, where investigators used a high-powered magnet to search storm drains along several streets.

Bernard testified that investigators removed the drain covers, lowered the magnet inside and swept connecting pipes before he physically climbed into accessible culverts with a flashlight to search areas the magnet may have missed.
They found nothing.
CHRISTIAN MOTHER, TEACHER'S AUTOPSY CONDUCTED AS POLICE PROBE HOMICIDE IN OHIO HOME INVASION

Investigators later had both vehicles from the Flynn home placed on lifts so they could search underneath them and other areas where something could have been hidden, Bernard testified. That search also came up empty.
Body camera footage shows Caleb Flynn bending down to vomit after his wife’s murder inside their home in Tipp City, Ohio on Feb. 16, 2026. (Tipp City Police Department)
Police even rented equipment to remove insulation from the attic as they continued looking for the gun.
Bernard testified that investigators also tried to trace Flynn's firearm purchase history after Flynn previously said he bought a gun in South Carolina, where he obtained his concealed-carry permit.
The detective said he called nearly two dozen gun stores in the state looking for records that could identify the make, model and serial number of a firearm purchased by Flynn.
That effort did not identify a gun tied to Flynn or Ashley.
The testimony came after a forensic pathologist walked jurors through Ashley's autopsy and described two gunshot wounds to the back of her head.

Dr. Bryan Casto testified that the entrance wounds overlapped, and the bullets traveled through Ashley's head on nearly parallel paths. One of the bullets exited her head before reentering her left arm near the elbow, where it was recovered during the autopsy.
Casto said the wounds and the paths of the bullets suggested Ashley was shot at close range, but he could not say exactly how far away the gun was when it was fired.
CHRISTIAN MOTHER, TEACHER FOUND DEAD AS POLICE HUNT HOMICIDE SUSPECT IN OHIO HOME INVASION
The pathologist determined Ashley died from multiple gunshot wounds to the head.

Earlier Monday, Ohio Bureau of Criminal Investigation (BCI) crime scene investigators walked jurors through evidence collected throughout the Flynn home as prosecutors sought to show the alleged break-in had been staged.
Ashley and Caleb Flynn in an undated photo with their two children. (GoFundMe)

A BCI crime scene technician who had examined between 20 and 30 forced-entry doors testified that the damage to a side garage door did not look like the forced entries she had previously investigated.
She said the damage was on the inside of the door rather than areas she would typically expect to be damaged if someone had kicked or pried their way inside.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Flynn's defense challenged the state's conclusions on cross-examination, pointing out that investigators could not determine when some of the door damage occurred and that no blood-spatter analysis was performed because conditions at the scene were not suitable for one.
Caleb Flynn in a 2013 "American Idol" Hometown Interview. Caleb is the husband of Ashley Flynn, who was shot and killed in her Ohio home on Monday, February 16, 2026. (YouTube/American Idol)
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
David Hammond, a senior special agent with BCI, also testified that he was not aware of evidence showing blood spatter from Ashley's shooting on Flynn's clothing.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE
The defense later pressed Bernard about tips received after the killing, including one from a caller who referenced an alleged "hit."
SEND US A TIP
Bernard testified that he printed tips received by Tipp City police and passed them to the FBI for follow-up. He said he did not know whether the FBI investigated that particular tip.
GOT A TIP?
The judge sustained objections when the defense tried to get into some of the caller's specific claims.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Prosecutors also laid the groundwork Monday for the massive trove of messages they say Flynn exchanged with his mistress.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
Bernard testified that a search warrant served on Microsoft produced 107,655 lines of data associated with an email address belonging to Flynn.

The records were admitted into evidence over a defense objection.

title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror's lawyer torches 'Looney Tunes motion' to investigate him
summary: Lindsay Clancy's defense seeks an investigation into the holdout juror, while his attorney fires back calling the motion an attack on the Constitution.
story: A mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy case prompts holdout juror Michael P. Desronvil to defend his position through a statement. Criminal defense attorney Mercedes Colwin breaks down the juror's reasoning and outlines potential next steps for prosecutors in Massachusetts, including a possible retrial or negotiated plea deal as the high-profile legal battle continues.

Lindsay Clancy's defense team is calling for an investigation into the holdout juror who sought to find her guilty of murder in the strangling of her children and using his refusal to bow to peer pressure to ask a judge to dismiss her charges — prompting a blistering response from his lawyer.

"The 'Looney Tunes' motion filed yesterday by Kevin 'Shooter McGavin' Reddington to investigate Michael is not just an attack on Michael for being the courageous lone holdout juror," attorney Edward Paltzik wrote on X Tuesday morning, referring to the holdout, Michael Desronvil.

"Reddington's motion is actually a full-frontal attack on the U.S. Constitution," Paltzik warned. "Because if the new normal is that jurors are going to face brutal reprisals for disagreeing with a defense attorney, you can kiss the Sixth Amendment goodbye."
LINDSAY CLANCY PROSECUTORS FACE DILEMMA: RETRIAL OR PLEA DEAL IN CASE INVOLVING 3 STRANGLED CHILDREN
Michael P. Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial, which ended in a mistrial. (Fugitive TV)
He warned that if the judge grants defense demands for an investigation into his client it would undermine the American criminal justice system in the long run.

"If we follow his destructive proposal to its logical conclusion, we're going to have an endless cycle of prosecutors investigating holdouts who oppose 'guilty' and defense attorneys investigating holdouts who oppose 'not guilty,'" he wrote. "Pretty soon we'll end up with... a retrograde justice system that will look a lot like the Hatfield-McCoy Feud: a cycle of carnage so malignant that its origins will fade in importance, replaced by the hopeless death spiral of the cycle itself."

Reddington, in a motion filed Friday, called for a "limited inquiry" into the holdout, for information about his background and potential criminal history, phone records, courthouse surveillance video and more.
Lindsay Clancy looks at jurors as Judge Sullivan asks them to start deliberations for a sixth day. The Lindsay Clancy jury resumes deliberations for a sixth day on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026. ( )
Neither Paltzik nor Reddington immediately responded to requests for comment from Fox News Digital Tuesday morning.
LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE CALLS MISTRIAL, THEN GRANTS DEFENSE ONE HOUR STAY FOR APPEAL

In a separate filing, another attorney for Clancy, Martin Weinberg, argued that Judge William Sullivan's decision to overrule a defense objection at trial should be grounds for dismissing the charges against the 36-year-old defendant on double jeopardy grounds. That motion also centered on the holdout juror and allegations that he ignored the judge's instructions and the law.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)

"The jury twice informed the Court that one of its members was refusing to apply the Court's instructions regarding the fundamental concept of reasonable doubt," Weinberg wrote. "After the first such report, the Court asked each juror individually whether he or she was able to apply the law. Upon receiving the second report, the Court tempered its response even further, simply reminding all jurors as a group of their obligation to follow its instructions generally. The Court denied Ms. Clancy's explicit requests to go further."

title: Texas prosecutors take death penalty off the table for man accused of murdering wife and fleeing to Italy
summary: Lee Gilley fled the United States to Italy using forged documents and a fake name after allegedly killing his pregnant wife in Harris County, Texas.
story: Anne Bremner, a Seattle trial lawyer was an advocate for Amanda Knox, explains why Lee Gilley's flight to Italy shielded him from the death penalty he faced in Texas.

Texas prosecutors announced they won't seek the death penalty against a man accused of killing his wife and fleeing the country as his trial was set to begin, they told an Italian court, clearing a path for his extradition to the United States.

Lee Gilley, 39, faces a capital murder charge in connection with the October 2024 death of his wife, Christa, who was nine weeks pregnant when she died. The Harris County Medical Examiner's office determined her death was a homicide resulting from neck compression. He pleaded not guilty.

Authorities allege Gilley removed his ankle monitor on May 1 and left Texas before his scheduled trial was to begin. He got to the Milan Malpensa Airport in Italy by using a fake name and forged travel documents, according to court records. He was taken into custody by Italian authorities.
EXCLUSIVE: FBI EXTRADITIONS SOAR AS PATEL RAMPS UP FOREIGN OUTREACH, VOWS 'NO SANCTUARY'

Lee Mongerson Gilley and his defense attorney, Ed McClees, right, are shown in the 497th District Court at the Harris County Justice Center, 1201 Franklin, Thursday, Oct. 17, 2024, in Houston. He is charged with capital murder in the death of his wife, Christa Gilley. (Melissa Phillip/Houston Chronicle via Getty Images)

Gilley's American attorney, Dick DeGuerin, previously told Fox News Digital that Italy wanted a written guarantee prosecutors wouldn't seek the death penalty before considering his return. Italian authorities may also demand assurances against a sentence of life without parole, he said.

The Harris County District Attorney said in a Friday court filing obtained by Fox News Digital that it won't be pursuing the death penalty against Gilley, but stopped short of taking life without parole off the table as a possible sentence.
MULTIPLE DEATH SENTENCES IN DIFFERENT STATES ARE SET TO BE CARRIED OUT WITHIN 24 HOURS: 'NOT VERY COMMON'

"Nevertheless, the State files this unusual notice because the defendant continues to falsely insist to the Court of Appeal of Turin that he remains subject to the death penalty, and that a judge or jury could assess the death penalty notwithstanding the State's decision not to seek that punishment," the filing states.

Harris County prosecutors also accused Gilley's Italian attorney, Monica Grosso, of misleading the Turin Court of Appeal by telling it that commutation is impossible for someone sentenced to life without parole.
CALIFORNIA SUED OVER POLICY THAT COULD FREE SERIAL KILLERS AS LACI PETERSON'S FRIEND SOUNDS ALARM
Lee Mongerson Gilley, 39, is accused of murdering his wife, Christa Bauer Gilley, and their unborn child in Houston in 2024, according to KPRC. (Christa Bauer Gilley/Facebook)

"Should he be sentenced to life without parole, the defendant would be eligible for commutation consideration," prosecutors said. "It is our hope that this notice will put an end to the defendant's charade so that he can be tried by a jury or judge in the United States and the victims receive the justice they deserve."
A hearing was held before the Turin Court of Appeal on Sept. 7. DeGuerin told Fox News Digital that Gilley's extradition was again delayed.
